units.zh: 列傳第二十二 羊欣張敷王微
units.en: Biography 22: Yang Xin, Zhang Fu, and Wang Wei
units.literal: Biography 22: Yang Xin, Zhang Fu, and Wang Wei

units.zh: 羊欣，字敬元，泰山南城人也。
units.en: Yang Xin, whose courtesy name was Jingyuan, came from Nancheng in Taishan commandery.
units.literal: Yang Xin, courtesy name Jingyuan, was a native of Nancheng in Taishan.

units.zh: 曾祖忱，晉徐州刺史。
units.en: His great-grandfather Chen had served as Inspector of Xu Province under the Jin.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Chen was Jin Inspector of Xu Province.

units.zh: 祖權，黃門郎。
units.en: His grandfather Quan had been a Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
units.literal: His grandfather Quan was a Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

units.zh: 父不疑，桂陽太守。
units.en: His father Buyi had been Governor of Guiyang.
units.literal: His father Buyi was Governor of Guiyang.

units.zh: 欣少靖默，無競於人，美言笑，善容止。
units.en: Xin had been quiet and unassuming since boyhood, never striving against others, with a pleasant wit and graceful bearing.
units.literal: From youth Xin was quiet and restrained, not competing with others; he had a fine manner of speech and laughter and was skilled in deportment.

units.zh: 汎覽經籍，尤長隸書。
units.en: He read widely in the classics and was especially masterful in clerical script calligraphy.
units.literal: He broadly read the classics and histories and was especially accomplished in clerical script.

units.zh: 不疑初為烏程令，欣時年十二，時王獻之為吳興太守，甚知愛之。
units.en: When Buyi first served as magistrate of Wucheng, Xin was twelve; Wang Xianzhi was then Governor of Wuxing and took a great liking to him.
units.literal: When Buyi was first magistrate of Wucheng, Xin was twelve; at the time Wang Xianzhi was Governor of Wuxing and greatly favored and cherished him.

units.zh: 獻之嘗夏月入縣，欣著新絹裙晝寢，獻之書裙數幅而去。
units.en: Once in midsummer Xianzhi came into the county seat; Xin was napping by day in a new silk gauze skirt, and Xianzhi wrote calligraphy across several panels of the skirt before departing.
units.literal: Xianzhi once entered the county in midsummer; Xin was wearing a new silk gauze skirt and napping by day; Xianzhi wrote several sections on the skirt and left.

units.zh: 欣本工書，因此彌善。
units.en: Xin had already been adept at calligraphy, and this episode made him still better.
units.literal: Xin was already skilled at writing; through this he became even more accomplished.

units.zh: 起家輔國參軍，府解還家。
units.en: He entered office as aide to the General Who Assists the State; when that post was abolished he went home.
units.literal: He began his career as aide to the General Who Assists the State; when the office was dissolved he returned home.

units.zh: 隆安中，朝廷漸亂，欣優遊私門，不復進仕。
units.en: During the Long'an years, as the court slipped into disorder, Xin lived at ease in private life and sought no further advancement.
units.literal: In the Long'an era the court grew increasingly turbulent; Xin enjoyed himself leisurely at home and did not advance in office again.

units.zh: 會稽王世子元顯每使欣書，常辭不奉命，元顯怒，乃以為其後軍府舍人。
units.en: Yuan Xian, heir of the Prince of Kuaiji, often pressed Xin to do calligraphy for him; Xin routinely refused, and in anger Yuan Xian made him registrar of his Rear Army staff.
units.literal: Yuan Xian, heir of the Prince of Kuaiji, often had Xin write for him; Xin regularly declined and did not obey; Yuan Xian was angry and therefore appointed him registrar in his Rear Army headquarters.

units.zh: 此職本用寒人，欣意貌恬然，不以高卑見色，論者稱焉。
units.en: The post was normally given to men of humble origin, yet Xin remained serene in manner and never altered his demeanor with rank; men of judgment praised him for it.
units.literal: This post was originally filled by men of low birth; Xin's bearing and expression were calm, and he showed no change of color according to rank high or low; commentators praised this.

units.zh: 欣嘗詣領軍將軍謝混，混拂席改服，然後見之。
units.en: Once when Xin called on General of the Guards Xie Hun, Hun first brushed the seat and changed his garments before receiving him.
units.literal: Xin once visited General of the Guards Xie Hun; Hun brushed the mat and changed his dress before then receiving him.

units.zh: 時混族子靈運在坐，退告族兄瞻曰：「望蔡見羊欣，遂易衣改席。」
units.en: Xie Lingyun, a kinsman of Hun's, was present; afterward he told his elder kinsman Zhan, "When Wangcai received Yang Xin, he changed his clothes and brushed the mat."
units.literal: At the time Hun's clansman Lingyun was seated there; he withdrew and told his clansman elder brother Zhan: "When Wangcai saw Yang Xin, he at once changed clothes and the mat."

units.zh: 欣由此益知名。
units.en: From that moment Xin's fame grew still greater.
units.literal: Through this Xin became still more renowned.

units.zh: 桓玄輔政，領平西將軍，以欣為平西參軍，仍轉主簿，參預機要。
units.en: When Huan Xuan held power as regent while also serving as General Who Pacifies the West, he appointed Xin as staff aide to that command, then made him chief clerk with access to confidential policy.
units.literal: Huan Xuan assisted in government, holding concurrently the post of General Who Pacifies the West; he made Xin aide under the Pacifying West command, then transferred him to chief clerk, with participation in confidential affairs.

units.zh: 欣欲自疏，時漏密事，玄覺其此意，愈重之，以為楚臺殿中郎。
units.en: Xin tried to keep his distance, and on one occasion leaked confidential matters; Xuan detected his intent yet esteemed him the more and appointed him Palace Attendant of the Chu Terrace.
units.literal: Xin wished to distance himself; at the time he leaked secret affairs; Xuan perceived this intention and valued him all the more, appointing him Palace Attendant of the Chu Terrace.

units.zh: 謂曰：「尚書政事之本，殿中禮樂所出。
units.en: He told him, "The Secretariat is the foundation of state business; the palace bureau is where ritual and music take their form.
units.literal: He said to him: "The Secretariat is the root of governmental affairs; the palace office is where ritual and music proceed from.

units.zh: 卿昔處股肱，方此為輕也。」
units.en: You once served at the heart of power—by comparison this may seem a lighter post."
units.literal: You formerly stood in the arm-and-thigh posts; compared with that this is rather light."

units.zh: 欣拜職少日，稱病自免，屏居里巷，十餘年不出。
units.en: Xin accepted the post for only a few days, then pleaded illness and resigned; he shut himself within his neighborhood and did not stir abroad for more than a decade.
units.literal: Xin took office for only a few days, claimed illness and resigned of his own accord, and lived in seclusion in his lane, not going out for more than ten years.

units.zh: 義熙中，弟徽被遇於高祖，高祖謂諮議參軍鄭鮮之曰：「羊徽一時美器，世論猶在兄後，恨不識之。」
units.en: During the Yixi years Xin's younger brother Hui won favor with Gaozu, who said to Staff Aide Zheng Xianzhi, "Yang Hui is a rare talent of our time; opinion still ranks him below his brother—I regret never having met the elder."
units.literal: In the Yixi era younger brother Hui received favor from Gaozu; Gaozu said to Consultation and Planning Staff Aide Zheng Xianzhi: "Yang Hui is for the age a fine vessel; public opinion still places him after his elder brother—I regret not knowing him."

units.zh: 即板欣補右將軍劉藩司馬，轉長史，中軍將軍道憐諮議參軍。
units.en: He at once commissioned Xin as Major on the staff of General of the Right Liu Fan, then chief clerk, and finally Consultation Staff Aide to General of the Central Army Daolian.
units.literal: He thereupon issued a fiat appointing Xin to fill the post of Major under General of the Right Liu Fan, then transferred him to chief clerk and Staff Aide for Consultation and Planning under General of the Central Army Daolian.

units.zh: 出為新安太守。
units.en: He was sent out as Governor of Xin'an.
units.literal: He went out to serve as Governor of Xin'an.

units.zh: 在郡四年，簡惠著稱。
units.en: He governed the prefecture four years and won renown for simple, humane rule.
units.literal: In the commandery for four years, he was famed for simplicity and kind grace.

units.zh: 除臨川王義慶輔國長史，廬陵王義真車騎諮議參軍，並不就。
units.en: Appointments followed as Chief Clerk on the staff of Prince of Linchuan Yiqing's Kingdom-Assisting command and as Consultation Aide on Prince of Luling Yizhen's Chariots and Cavalry staff, but he took neither post.
units.literal: He was removed from office to become Chief Clerk for the Kingdom-Assisting Army under Prince of Linchuan Yiqing, and Consultation Staff Aide to the Chariots and Cavalry under Prince of Luling Yizhen—he accepted neither.

units.zh: 太祖重之，以為新安太守，前後凡十三年，遊玩山水，甚得適性。
units.en: Taizu esteemed him and again made him Governor of Xin'an; over thirteen years in all he wandered among hills and streams to his heart's content.
units.literal: Taizu valued him and appointed him Governor of Xin'an; altogether before and after thirteen years, he toured mountains and waters and greatly suited his nature.

units.zh: 轉在義興，非其好也。
units.en: When he was transferred to Yixing, it was not what he wanted.
units.literal: He was transferred to serve in Yixing—it was not to his liking.

units.zh: 頃之，又稱病篤自免歸。
units.en: Before long he again pleaded grave illness and resigned to go home.
units.literal: Shortly thereafter he again claimed serious illness and resigned to return home.

units.zh: 除中散大夫。
units.en: He was appointed Grand Master of Leisurely Disposition.
units.literal: He was removed from office and made Grand Master of Leisurely Disposition.

units.zh: 素好黃老，常手自書章，有病不服藥，飲符水而已。
units.en: He had long favored Daoist teachings, copied ritual texts himself, and when ill refused medicine, drinking only consecrated talisman water.
units.literal: He had long favored Huang-Lao teaching, often personally copying talismanic texts; when ill he did not take medicine but drank only talisman water.

units.zh: 兼善醫術，撰《藥方》十卷。
units.en: He was also skilled in medicine and compiled a ten-juan work titled Pharmaceutical Formulations.
units.literal: He was also skilled in medicine and compiled ten juan of Pharmaceutical Formulations.

units.zh: 欣以不堪拜伏，辭不朝覲，高祖、太祖並恨不識之。
units.en: Unable to endure prostration, Xin declined court audiences; both Gaozu and Taizu regretted never having met him in person.
units.literal: Because Xin could not bear to bow prostrate, he declined court audiences; both Gaozu and Taizu regretted never having met him.

units.zh: 自非尋省近親，不妄行詣，行必由城外，未嘗入六關。
units.en: Except for brief visits to near kin, he would not pay calls indiscriminately; when he traveled he always kept outside the city walls and never passed through the six inner gates.
units.literal: Unless visiting close kin on brief family business, he did not go about paying calls rashly; when traveling he always went by way outside the city and never entered the six passes.

units.zh: 元嘉十九年，卒，時年七十三。
units.en: He died in the nineteenth year of Yuanjia, at the age of seventy-three.
units.literal: In the nineteenth year of Yuanjia he died, aged seventy-three.

units.zh: 子俊，早卒。
units.en: His son Jun died young.
units.literal: His son Jun died young.

units.zh: 弟徽，字敬猷，世譽多欣。
units.en: His younger brother Hui, courtesy name Jingyou; worldly praise mostly favored Xin.
units.literal: Younger brother Hui, courtesy name Jingyou; worldly praise mostly favored Xin.

units.zh: 高祖鎮京口，以為記室參軍掌事。
units.en: When Gaozu was stationed at Jingkou, he made Hui Record-House Staff Aide in charge of affairs.
units.literal: When Gaozu held Jingkou, he made him Record-House Staff Aide in charge of affairs.

units.zh: 八年，遷中書郎，直西省。
units.en: In the eighth year he was promoted to Palace Gentleman on duty in the Western Secretariat.
units.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to Palace Gentleman and attended the Western Office.

units.zh: 後為太祖西中郎長史、河東太守。
units.en: He later became Chief Clerk on Taizu's Western Center Army staff and Governor of Hedong.
units.literal: Later he served as Chief Clerk of Taizu's Western Center Army and Governor of Hedong.

units.zh: 子瞻，元嘉末為世祖南中郎長史、尋陽太守，卒官。
units.en: His son Zhan, late in Yuanjia, was Chief Clerk on Shizu's Southern Center Army staff and Governor of Xunyang, and died in office.
units.literal: His son Zhan, at the end of Yuanjia served as Chief Clerk of Shizu's Southern Center Army and Governor of Xunyang, and died in office.

units.zh: 張敷，字景胤，吳郡人，吳興太守邵子也。
units.en: Zhang Fu, courtesy name Jingyin, was from Wu commandery and the son of Shao, Governor of Wuxing.
units.literal: Zhang Fu, courtesy name Jingyin, a man of Wu commandery, was the son of Governor of Wuxing Shao.

units.zh: 生而母沒。
units.en: His mother died when he was born.
units.literal: At birth his mother was gone.

units.zh: 年數歲，問母所在，家人告以死生之分，敷雖童蒙，便有思慕之色。
units.en: When he was only a few years old he asked where his mother was; the family explained that she had died; even as a small child Fu's face showed mourning and longing.
units.literal: At several years of age he asked where his mother was; the household told him of the division between life and death; though still a child, Fu already showed the color of longing and grief.

units.zh: 年十許歲，求母遺物，而散施已盡，唯得一畫扇，乃緘錄之，每至感思，輒開笥流涕。
units.en: Around ten he searched for keepsakes of his mother, but nearly everything had been given away; only one painted fan remained, which he wrapped and stored; whenever grief overtook him he opened the case and wept.
units.literal: At about ten he sought his mother's surviving objects, but what had been distributed was already exhausted; he obtained only one painted fan, which he sealed and kept; whenever moved to remembrance he would open the chest and weep.

units.zh: 見從母，常悲感哽咽。
units.en: Seeing his aunt by marriage always left him choked with sorrow.
units.literal: When he saw his maternal aunt he was often moved to grief and choked with sobs.

units.zh: 性整貴，風韻甚高，好讀玄書，兼屬文論，少有盛名。
units.en: Upright and fastidious by nature, with a lofty air, he loved metaphysical texts and wrote literary essays as well; his reputation was great even while young.
units.literal: By nature he was upright and noble; his bearing was very lofty; he loved reading arcane books and also composed literary disquisitions; from youth he had great fame.

units.zh: 高祖見而愛之，以為世子中軍參軍，數見接引。
units.en: Gaozu took him in at once and made him aide on the Heir Apparent's Central Army staff, summoning him often.
units.literal: Gaozu saw him and cherished him, making him aide to the Heir Apparent's Central Army, and many times received and guided him.

units.zh: 永初初，遷秘書郎。
units.en: Early in the Yongchu reign he was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman.
units.literal: At the beginning of Yongchu he was transferred to Secretariat Gentleman.

units.zh: 嘗在省直，中書令傅亮貴宿權要，聞其好學，過候之；
units.en: Once while on duty in the Secretariat, Chief Palace Attendant Fu Liang, a senior wielder of power, heard of his devotion to study and paid a visit;
units.literal: Once while on duty in the office, Palace Attendant Fu Liang, an elder of rank and power, heard of his love of learning and came calling;

units.zh: 敷臥不即起，亮怪而去。
units.en: Fu remained lying down and did not rise promptly; Liang took offense and withdrew.
units.literal: Fu was lying down and did not rise at once; Liang thought it strange and left.

units.zh: 父邵為湘州，去官侍從。
units.en: When his father Shao went to Xiang Province, Fu left his post to accompany him.
units.literal: His father Shao was assigned to Xiang Province; Fu left office to attend him.

units.zh: 太祖版為西中郎參軍。
units.en: Taizu commissioned him as aide on the Western Center Army staff.
units.literal: Taizu issued a fiat appointing him aide to the Western Center Army.

units.zh: 元嘉初，為員外散騎侍郎，秘書丞。
units.en: Early in Yuanjia he became Supernumerary Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Secretariat Director.
units.literal: Early in Yuanjia he served as Supernumerary Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Secretariat Director.

units.zh: 江夏王義恭鎮江陵，以為撫軍功曹，轉記室參軍。
units.en: When Prince of Jiangxia Yigong was stationed at Jiangling, he made Fu Merit Officer on his Pacification Army staff, then Record-House Staff Aide.
units.literal: Prince of Jiangxia Yigong held Jiangling and made him Merit Officer of the Pacification Army, then Record-House Staff Aide.

units.zh: 時義恭就太祖求一學義沙門，比沙門求見發遣，會敷赴假還江陵，太祖謂沙門曰：「張敷應西，當令相載。」
units.en: Yigong had asked Taizu for a learned monk; as the monk awaited travel orders, Fu was returning from leave to Jiangling; Taizu told the monk, "Zhang Fu is heading west—you may travel with him."
units.literal: At the time Yigong asked Taizu for a monk versed in doctrine; when that monk requested an interview for dispatch, it happened that Fu was returning from leave to Jiangling; Taizu said to the monk: "Zhang Fu is going west—you should have him carry you along."

units.zh: 及敷辭，上謂曰：「撫軍須一意懷道人，卿可以後艑載之，道中可得言晤。」
units.en: When Fu came to bid farewell, the Emperor said, "The Pacification Army wants a devoted man of religion—you may take him on the rear vessel and converse with him on the journey."
units.literal: When Fu came to take leave, the Emperor said to him: "The Pacification Army needs a single-minded man of the Way—you can carry him on the rear boat; on the road you may gain conversation together."

units.zh: 敷不奉旨，曰：「臣性不耐雜。」
units.en: Fu declined: "By nature I cannot abide mixed company."
units.literal: Fu did not obey the order and said: "By nature your subject cannot bear disorder."

units.zh: 上甚不說。
units.en: The Emperor was deeply displeased.
units.literal: The Emperor was greatly displeased.

units.zh: 遷正員郎。
units.en: He was promoted to Regular Gentleman.
units.literal: He was transferred to Regular Gentleman.

units.zh: 中書舍人狄當、周赳並管要務，以敷同省名家，欲詣之。
units.en: Palace Attendants Di Dang and Zhou Jiu, both handling weighty business, wished to call on Fu as a fellow officer from a great house.
units.literal: Palace Secretariat Attendants Di Dang and Zhou Jiu both managed important affairs; because Fu was of an eminent lineage in the same office, they wished to call on him.

units.zh: 赳曰：「彼若不相容，便不如不往。
units.en: Jiu said, "If he will not have us, we had best not go at all.
units.literal: Jiu said: "If he will not tolerate us, we had better not go.

units.zh: 詎可輕往邪？」
units.en: How can we presume to visit rashly?"
units.literal: How can one go lightly?"

units.zh: 當曰：「吾等並已員外郎矣，何憂不得共坐。」
units.en: Dang said, "We are both already supernumerary gentlemen—why fear we cannot sit together?"
units.literal: Dang said: "We are both already Supernumerary Gentlemen—why worry that we cannot share a seat?"

units.zh: 敷先設二床，去壁三四尺，二客就席，酬接甚歡，既而呼左右曰：「移我遠客。」
units.en: Fu set out two couches several feet from the wall; the visitors sat down and conversation went pleasantly—then he ordered his servants, "Move my distant guests farther off."
units.literal: Fu first set out two couches three or four feet from the wall; the two guests took their seats and the exchange was very pleasant; then he called to his attendants: "Move my distant guests away."

units.zh: 赳等失色而去。
units.en: Jiu and the rest blanched and withdrew.
units.literal: Jiu and the others changed color and left.

units.zh: 其自摽遇如此。
units.en: Such was the pride with which he held himself.
units.literal: Thus were his own standards of treatment.

units.zh: 善持音儀，盡詳緩之致，與人別，執手曰：「念相聞。」
units.en: He carried voice and bearing to the utmost in unhurried grace; when parting he would take one's hand and say, "Remember to send word."
units.literal: He was skilled in maintaining tone and deportment, exhausting every grace of measured calm; when parting from someone he would clasp hands and say: "Think of keeping in touch."

units.zh: 餘響久之不絕。
units.en: The cadence of his voice would linger long afterward.
units.literal: The lingering resonance long did not cease.

units.zh: 張氏後進至今慕之，其源流起自敷也。
units.en: Younger members of the Zhang clan still emulate him today; the family style begins with Fu.
units.literal: Later generations of the Zhang house still admire this to the present; the stream and source begin with Fu.

units.zh: 遷黃門侍郎，始興王濬後軍長史，司徒左長史。
units.en: He was promoted to Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, Chief Clerk on Prince of Shixing Jun's Rear Army staff, and Left Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works.
units.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, Chief Clerk of Prince of Shixing Jun's Rear Army, and Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.

units.zh: 未拜，父在吳興亡，報以疾篤，敷往奔省，自發都至吳興成服，凡十餘日，始進水漿。
units.en: Before he could assume the post his father died in Wuxing; hearing he was gravely ill, Fu hurried home; from leaving the capital until donning mourning dress in Wuxing took more than ten days, and only then did he take his first water and gruel.
units.literal: Before taking office his father died in Wuxing; a report came that he was gravely ill; Fu rushed to attend him; from leaving the capital to donning mourning garments in Wuxing altogether more than ten days, only then did he first take water gruel.

units.zh: 葬畢，不進鹽菜，遂毀瘠成疾。
units.en: After the burial he ate neither salt nor vegetables and wasted away until illness took hold.
units.literal: When the burial was complete he took no salt or vegetables and thus wasted away into illness.

units.zh: 世父茂度每止譬之，輒更感慟，絕而復續。
units.en: His uncle Maodu repeatedly tried to comfort him, but each time Fu only grieved the more, fainting and coming round again.
units.literal: His father's elder brother Maodu constantly tried to check and comfort him; Fu would be moved to grief again, fainting and reviving by turns.

units.zh: 茂度曰：「我冀譬汝有益，但更甚耳。」
units.en: Maodu said, "I hoped consolation would help you, but it has only deepened your grief."
units.literal: Maodu said: "I hoped comfort would benefit you, but it has only made it worse."

units.zh: 自是不復往。
units.en: After that he ceased visiting altogether.
units.literal: From then on he did not go again.

units.zh: 未朞而卒，時年四十一。
units.en: He died before the mourning year was out, at forty-one.
units.literal: Before the mourning period was complete he died, aged forty-one.

units.zh: 琅邪顏延之書弔茂度曰：「賢弟子少履貞規，長懷理要，清風素氣，得之天然。
units.en: Yan Yanzhi of Langye wrote Maodu a letter of condolence: "Your worthy nephew practiced integrity from youth and held to essential truth in maturity; clarity of spirit was his by nature.
units.literal: Yan Yanzhi of Langye wrote to condole with Maodu: "Your worthy nephew from youth trod the path of pure rule, in maturity cherished essential principle, clear wind and plain spirit—he gained these from Heaven's endowment.

units.zh: 言面以來，便申忘年之好，比雖艱隔成阻，而情問無睽。
units.en: From our first meeting we formed a friendship without regard to age; though distance has lately intervened, our bond has not cooled.
units.literal: Since we spoke face to face he extended the friendship that forgets years; though recently hardship and separation have formed barriers, our emotional exchange has known no breach.

units.zh: 薄莫之人，冀其方見慰說，豈謂中年，奄為長往，聞問悼心，有兼恆痛。
units.en: I am a man in life's twilight and hoped soon to enjoy his company again—who dreamed that in his prime he would be gone so suddenly? The news fills me with grief beyond ordinary sorrow.
units.literal: A man in the dusk of life, I hoped soon to see comfort and discourse—who would have thought that in midlife he would suddenly make the long journey? Hearing the news my grieving heart shares in constant pain.

units.zh: 足下門教敦至，兼實家寶，一旦喪失，何可為懷。」
units.en: Your family discipline is exemplary, and he was its jewel; to lose him in a day—how can the heart bear it?"
units.literal: Your household instruction is thick and perfect, and he was moreover a true treasure of the family; in one morning lost—how can it be borne in the breast?"

units.zh: 其見重如此。
units.en: Such was the esteem in which men held him.
units.literal: Thus was the esteem in which he was held.

units.zh: 世祖即位，詔曰：「司徒故左長史張敷，貞心簡立，幼樹風規。
units.en: When Emperor Shizu ascended the throne, an edict read: "The late Zhang Fu, former Left Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works, bore a loyal heart and plain integrity and established his moral bearing from youth.
units.literal: When Shizu took the throne an edict said: "Former Left Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works Zhang Fu—loyal heart, plain establishment; from youth he planted wind and rule.

units.zh: 居哀毀滅，孝道淳至，宜在追甄，於以報美。
units.en: In mourning he destroyed himself—filial devotion of the purest kind; let posthumous honors recall his excellence.
units.literal: In mourning he destroyed himself—filial devotion pure and utmost; he should receive posthumous advancement, thereby to repay his excellence.

units.zh: 可追贈侍中。」
units.en: Let him be posthumously awarded Palace Attendant."
units.literal: He may be posthumously awarded Palace Attendant."

units.zh: 於是改其所居稱為孝張里。
units.en: His former neighborhood was thereafter renamed Filial Zhang Lane.
units.literal: Thereupon his former residence was renamed Filial Zhang Lane.

units.zh: 無子。
units.en: He left no sons.
units.literal: He had no sons.

units.zh: 王微，字景玄，琅邪臨沂人，太保弘弟子也。
units.en: Wang Wei, courtesy name Jingxuan, was from Linyi in Langye and a nephew of Grand Mentor Wang Hong.
units.literal: Wang Wei, courtesy name Jingxuan, a native of Linyi in Langye, was the younger son of the younger brother of Grand Mentor Hong.

units.zh: 父孺，光祿大夫。
units.en: His father Ru was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
units.literal: His father Ru was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

units.zh: 微少好學，無不通覽，善屬文，能書畫，兼解音律、醫方、陰陽術數。
units.en: From youth Wei loved learning and read broadly; he wrote well, painted and practiced calligraphy, and knew music, medicine, and the arts of yin-yang and prognostication.
units.literal: From youth Wei loved learning and there was nothing he did not read through; he was skilled at literary composition, could write and paint, and also understood music, medical prescriptions, and yin-yang numerology.

units.zh: 年十六，州舉秀才，衡陽王義季右軍參軍，並不就。
units.en: At sixteen the province nominated him as Cultivated Talent and Prince of Hengyang Yiji made him aide on the Right Army staff—he took neither post.
units.literal: At sixteen the province recommended him as Cultivated Talent; aide to the Right Army under Prince of Hengyang Yiji—he accepted neither.

units.zh: 起家司徒祭酒，轉主簿，始興王濬後軍功曹記室參軍，太子中舍人，始興王友。
units.en: He entered office as Libationer of the Minister of Works, then chief clerk, Merit Officer and Record-House Aide on Prince of Shixing Jun's Rear Army staff, Attendant in the Heir Apparent's household, and Friend to the Prince of Shixing.
units.literal: He began his career as Libationer of the Minister of Works, became chief clerk, Merit Officer and Record-House Staff Aide in Prince of Shixing Jun's Rear Army, Attendant in the Household of the Heir Apparent, and Friend to the Prince of Shixing.

units.zh: 父憂去官，服闋，除南平王鑠右軍諮議參軍。
units.en: He left office for his father's mourning; when the period ended he was appointed Consultation Aide on Prince of Nanping Shuo's Right Army staff.
units.literal: On his father's death he left office; when mourning was complete he was appointed Consultation Staff Aide to the Right Army under Prince of Nanping Shuo.

units.zh: 微素無宦情，稱疾不就。
units.en: Wei had never sought office and pleaded illness rather than accept.
units.literal: Wei had never had desire for office; he claimed illness and did not accept.

units.zh: 仍除中書侍郎，又擬南琅邪、義興太守，並固辭。
units.en: Appointments followed as Palace Gentleman and as Governor of Southern Langye and Yixing—but he firmly declined them all.
units.literal: He was still removed and made Palace Gentleman of the Secretariat; he was also slated for Governor of Southern Langye and Governor of Yixing—he firmly declined all.

units.zh: 吏部尚書江湛舉微為吏部郎，微與湛書曰：
units.en: Minister of Personnel Jiang Zhan nominated Wei as Director of the Ministry of Personnel; Wei wrote him:
units.literal: Minister of Personnel Jiang Zhan recommended Wei as Director of the Ministry of Personnel; Wei wrote to Zhan saying:

units.zh: 弟心病亂度，非但蹇蹙而已，此處朝野所共知。
units.en: Your younger brother suffers a disordered heart, not mere lameness—that is known to court and countryside alike.
units.literal: Your younger brother's heart illness is a disorder of confusion, not merely lameness and constriction—this the court and countryside together know.

units.zh: 騶會忽扣蓽門，閭里咸以為祥怪，君多識前世之載，天值何其易傾。
units.en: Outriders suddenly knocked at my humble door; neighbors took it for a portent. You who have read the records of former ages know how easily Heaven's favor can overturn.
units.literal: Outriders suddenly knocked at my humble gate; neighbors all took it for an omen strange or ill—you who have read much of former ages' records, how easily Heaven's appointment can topple!

units.zh: 弟受海內駭笑，不過如燕石禿鶖邪，未知君何以自解於良史邪？
units.en: Your younger brother will become a laughingstock throughout the realm—no better than the stone goose or the bald ibis, perhaps. How will you answer the impartial historian?
units.literal: Your younger brother will receive the empire's startled laughter—no more than goose-stone or a bald osprey, is it not? I do not know how you will explain yourself to the good historian.

units.zh: 今雖王道鴻鬯，或有激朗於天表，必欲探援潛寶，傾海求珠，自可卜肆巫祠之間，馬棧牛口之下，賞劇孟於博徒，拔卜式於芻牧。
units.en: Though the royal way now flourishes, men of brilliance may still appear from on high; if you wish to seek hidden talent and pearls from the deep, you may find them between the fortune-teller's stall and the shaman's shrine, in the stable and the cattle pen—as when Ju Meng was valued among gamblers or Bu Shi was drawn up from the pasture.
units.literal: Though the royal way now flourishes and spreads, there may be those stirred to brilliance above the heavens; if one must probe and draw forth hidden treasures and tilt the sea to seek pearls, one may between diviner's stalls and shaman shrines, beneath horse lodges and ox mouths, reward Ju Meng among gamblers and raise up Bu Shi from cattle tending.

units.zh: 亦有西戎孤臣，東都戒士，上窮範馳之御，下盡詭遇之能，兼鱗雜襲者，必不乏於世矣。
units.en: Western frontier exiles and eastern capital veterans abound—men who master charioteering at one extreme and cunning stratagem at the other; the world is never short of men who combine many talents.
units.literal: There are also isolated subjects of the western borderlands, guardians from the eastern capital, exhausting at the top the driving of Fan and Chi and at the bottom all the skills of crafty encounter; those with both scales mixed and overlapping must certainly not be lacking in the world.

units.zh: 且廬於承明，署乎金馬，皆明察之官，又賢於管庫之末。
units.en: The scholars lodged at Chenming and posted at the Golden Horse Gate are all men of keen judgment—far worthier than a post at the bottom of the granary rolls.
units.literal: Moreover those lodged at Chenming and posted at Golden Horse are all officials of clear scrutiny, again more worthy than the lowest post of keeper of stores.

units.zh: 何為劫勒通家疾病人，塵穢難堪之選，將以靖國，不亦益囂乎？
units.en: Why force upon the state a sick man from a great family, a choice foul and unfit, in the name of good government—would that not only make matters worse?
units.literal: Why forcibly press a man of an allied house who is ill, a choice filthy and unbearable, intending to pacify the state—is it not the more to increase clamor?

units.zh: 《書》云：「任官維賢才」。
units.en: The Documents says, "In appointing officials, set merit and talent first."
units.literal: The Documents says: "In appointing officials, set merit and talent first."

units.zh: 而君擢士先疹廢，芃芃棫樸，似不如此。
units.en: Yet you choose officials by starting with the sick and broken—the ode's thriving saplings were not chosen that way.
units.literal: Yet you promote men beginning with those wasted by rash and illness—the luxuriant elm saplings do not seem to be thus.

units.zh: 且弟曠違兄姊，迄將十載，姊時歸來，終不任輿曳入閣，兄守金城，永不堪扶抱就路，若不憊疾，非性僻而何。
units.en: Your younger brother has been away from his siblings nearly ten years; when my sister visits I cannot endure being carried in a carriage through the gate; my brother holds Jincheng and I can never bear being helped along the road—if this is not illness, what else could it be but a perverse nature?
units.literal: Moreover your younger brother has been absent from elder brother and sisters nearly ten years; when sister returned, I could never bear to be dragged in a carriage into the gate; elder brother guards Jincheng, forever unable to bear being supported on the road—if this is not weariness of illness, what is perverse nature?

units.zh: 比君曰表裏，無假長目飛耳也。
units.en: When you speak of knowing a man inside and out, you need no spies with far-reaching eyes and ears.
units.literal: When you speak of inner and outer, there is no need for long eyes and flying ears.

units.zh: 常謂生遭太公，將即華士之戮；
units.en: I have often said that had I lived in the age of the Grand Duke of Qi, I would soon have shared Hua Shi's fate;
units.literal: I have often said that if born in the age of the Grand Duke, I would soon meet the execution of the Flower Gentleman;

units.zh: 幸遇管叔，必蒙僻儒之養。
units.en: had I met Uncle Guan instead, I would surely have been kept alive as an eccentric scholar.
units.literal: fortunate to meet Uncle Guan, I would surely receive the fostering of an eccentric scholar.

units.zh: 光武以馮衍才浮其實，故棄而不齒。
units.en: Emperor Guangwu found Feng Yan's talent greater than his substance and cast him aside without a place at court.
units.literal: Emperor Guangwu, because Feng Yan's talent floated above his substance, cast him aside and did not rank him among his teeth.

units.zh: 諸葛孔明云：「來敏亂郡，過於孔文舉。」
units.en: Zhuge Liang said, "Lai Min throws a commandery into disorder—worse than Kong Rong."
units.literal: Zhuge Kongming said: "Lai Min throws a commandery into disorder, exceeding Kong Wenju."

units.zh: 況無古人之才槩，敢干周、漢之常刑。
units.en: How much less do I possess the capacity of the ancients, yet dare to invite the ordinary penalties of Zhou and Han!
units.literal: How much more when one lacks the capacity of the ancients yet dares to offend against the regular punishments of Zhou and Han!

units.zh: 彼二三英賢，足為曉治與否？
units.en: Do those two or three worthy men suffice to show whether one understands good government?
units.literal: Are those two or three worthy men enough to show understanding of governance or not?

units.zh: 恐君逄此時，或亦不免高閣，乃復假名不知己者，豈欲自比衛賜邪？
units.en: I fear that in such a time you too may not escape disgrace in high office, yet you borrow the name of one who does not know you—do you wish to compare yourself to Wei Ci?
units.literal: I fear that when you meet such a time you likewise may not escape the high pavilion; yet you borrow a name from one who does not know you—do you wish to compare yourself to Wei Ci?

units.zh: 君欲高斅山公，而以仲容見處，徒以搥提禮學，本不參選，鄙夫瞻彼，固不任下走，未知新沓何如州陵耳。
units.en: You wish to take Mount Gong as your model yet treat me like Ruan Zhongrong; raised on ritual learning, I was never on the selection rolls—a coarse man like me cannot serve as your runner, and I do not know how the new appointee compares with you, Zhouling.
units.literal: You wish to imitate high Mount Gong, yet treat me as Zhongrong; merely because I was raised on ritual learning I was never in the selection lists—this coarse fellow looking on that naturally cannot serve as a runner; I do not know what the new entrant is like compared with Zhouling.

units.zh: 而作不師古，坐亂官政，誣飾蚯蚓，冀招神龍，如復託以真素者，又不宜居華留名，有害風俗。
units.en: Yet acting without antiquity as your guide you disturb official government, dressing up an earthworm and hoping to summon a dragon; if one truly relies on plain authenticity, one should not dwell in glory and leave a name—harmful to custom.
units.literal: Yet acting without taking antiquity as teacher you disturb official government, bedecking an earthworm and hoping to summon a divine dragon; if one again relies on plain authenticity, one should not dwell in glory and leave a name—harmful to custom.

units.zh: 君亦不至期人如此，若交以為人賜，舉未以己勞，則商販之事，又連所不忍聞也。
units.en: You should not expect such a man either; if friendship is treated as a gift from others and promotion comes without one's own effort—that is merchant's business, and something I cannot bear to hear.
units.literal: You also should not expect a man so; if association is taken as a gift from others, and promotion without one's own labor—then the affairs of merchants, again something one cannot bear to hear.

units.zh: 豈謂不肖易擢，貪者可誘，凡此數者，君必居一焉。
units.en: Do you mean that the unworthy are easy to promote and the greedy can be bought—of all these you must be guilty of at least one.
units.literal: Do you mean that the unworthy are easy to promote and the greedy can be enticed—of all these several you must occupy one.

units.zh: 雖假天口於齊駢，藉鬼說於周季，公孫碎毛髮之文，莊生縱漭瀁之極，終不能舉其契，為之辭矣。
units.en: Though one had the eloquence of the Qi persuaders, the ghost lore of late Zhou, Gongsun Long's hair-splitting disputations, or Zhuangzi's boundless paradoxes, one still could not justify this appointment.
units.literal: Though one borrow Heaven's mouth from the Qi persuader, borrow ghostly discourse from the Zhou season, Gongsun split the essay of hair and down, Zhuangzi let the vast flood to its extreme—still one cannot raise their bond and make excuse for it.

units.zh: 子將明魂，必靈咍於萬里，汝、潁餘彥，將拂衣而不朝。
units.en: Zizhan's bright spirit must laugh in the dark from afar; the remaining fine men of Ru and Ying will brush their robes and refuse court.
units.literal: Zizhan's bright soul must laugh darkly at ten thousand li; the remaining fine men of Ru and Ying will brush their coats and not attend court.

units.zh: 浮華一開，風俗或從此而爽。
units.en: Once ostentation is unleashed, custom may slip away from this.
units.literal: Once ostentation opens, custom may from this slip away.

units.zh: 鬼谷以揣情為最難，何君忖度之輕謬。
units.en: Guiguzi held gauging a man's heart the hardest art—how lightly and absurdly you judge!
units.literal: Guiguzi held gauging sentiment the hardest—how lightly and absurdly you estimate!

units.zh: 今有此書，非敢叨擬中散，誠不能顧影負心，純盜虛聲，所以綿絡累紙，本不營尚書虎爪板也。
units.en: This letter is not written to imitate Ji Kang; I truly cannot look at my shadow and betray my heart or steal empty fame; these pages are strung together because I never sought the Ministry's appointment tablet.
units.literal: Now having this letter, I do not dare presumptuously to imitate the Master of Dispersal; truly I cannot look at my shadow and betray my heart, purely stealing empty fame; therefore these pages strung together—I never schemed for the Ministry's tiger-claw board.

units.zh: 成童便往來居舍，晨省復經周旋，加有諸甥，亦何得頓絕慶弔。
units.en: Since childhood I have visited family homes for morning calls and social rounds; with many nephews besides, how can I abruptly cut off congratulations and condolence?
units.literal: From childhood I have gone back and forth to residences; morning calls and again social rounds—with many nephews besides, how can one abruptly cut off congratulations and condolence?

units.zh: 然生平之意，自於此都盡。
units.en: Yet the purpose of my life ends here entirely.
units.literal: Yet the intent of my lifetime ends here entirely.

units.zh: 君平公云：「生我名者殺我身。」
units.en: Lord Junping said, "He who gives me fame kills my person."
units.literal: Lord Junping said: "He who gives me fame kills my person."

units.zh: 天爵且猶滅名，安用吏部郎哉！
units.en: Heavenly honor already destroys one's name—what use is the post of Director of the Ministry of Personnel!
units.literal: Heavenly ennoblement already extinguishes name—what use is Director of the Ministry of Personnel!

units.zh: 其舉可陋，其事不經，非獨搢紳者不道，僕妾皆將咲之。
units.en: This recommendation is contemptible and the affair irregular; not only will the gentry refuse to speak of it—even servants and concubines will laugh.
units.literal: This recommendation is contemptible, this affair uncanonical; not only will gentry not speak of it—servants and concubines will all laugh.

units.zh: 忽忽不樂，自知壽不得長，且使千載知弟不詐諼耳。
units.en: Restless and unhappy, I know my years will not be long; yet let a thousand years know your younger brother does not lie.
units.literal: Restless and unhappy, I know my years will not be long; yet let a thousand years know your younger brother does not feign falsely.

units.zh: 微既為始興王濬府吏，濬數相存慰，微奉答箋書，輒飾以辭采。
units.en: Once Wei became an officer on Prince of Shixing Jun's staff, Jun often sent words of concern; Wei in his replies always adorned his letters with literary polish.
units.literal: Wei having become an officer in Prince of Shixing Jun's headquarters, Jun many times sent words of concern; Wei in replying memorials always adorned them with literary color.

units.zh: 微為文古甚，頗抑揚，袁淑見之，謂為訴屈。
units.en: Wei's style was very archaic and heavily modulated; Yuan Shu, reading it, said it sounded like a complaint of wrongs suffered.
units.literal: Wei's writing was very antique, with much modulation and cadence; Yuan Shu reading it said it was lodging grievance.

units.zh: 微因此又與從弟僧綽書曰：
units.en: Wei therefore wrote to his younger cousin Sengchuo:
units.literal: Wei therefore also wrote to his younger cousin Sengchuo saying:

units.zh: 吾雖無人鑒，要是早知弟，每共宴語，前言何嘗不以止足為貴。
units.en: Though I am no judge of men, I have known you long; whenever we talked at leisure, did we not always prize knowing when to stop?
units.literal: Though I have no mirror of men, I have known you early; whenever we feasted and spoke together, in former words how did we not take knowing when to stop as precious?

units.zh: 且持盈畏滿，自是家門舊風，何為一旦落漠至此，當局苦迷，將不然邪！
units.en: Holding fast when full and fearing excess is our family's old way—why have you fallen to such desolation in a single day? Those in charge are deeply deluded—are they not!
units.literal: Moreover holding fullness and fearing surfeit is itself the old wind of our house—why in one morning fall to such desolation? Those in charge are bitterly deluded—will it not be so!

units.zh: 詎容都不先聞，或可不知耳。
units.en: Could you not have told me first—or perhaps you did not know.
units.literal: How could it be tolerated that you did not inform me first—or perhaps you did not know.

units.zh: 衣冠胄胤，如吾者甚多，才能固不足道，唯不傾側溢詐，士頗以此容之。
units.en: There are many scions of great houses like me; my talent is nothing to speak of—only in not leaning and overflowing with deceit do gentlemen somewhat tolerate me.
units.literal: Capped and belted descendants like me are many; talent and ability are certainly not worth speaking of—only in not leaning and overflowing with deceit do gentlemen somewhat tolerate me for this.

units.zh: 至於規矩細行，難可詳料。
units.en: As for rules of conduct and small proprieties, these are hard to reckon in detail.
units.literal: As for rules and minute conduct, it is hard to reckon in detail.

units.zh: 疹疾日滋，縱恣益甚，人道所貴，廢不復脩。
units.en: My rash illness grows daily and my indulgence ever worse; what human conduct esteems I have abandoned and no longer cultivate.
units.literal: Rash illness daily increases, indulgence and license ever more severe; what human conduct esteems I abandon and no longer cultivate.

units.zh: 幸值聖明相容，置之教外，且舊恩所及，每蒙寬假。
units.en: Fortunately a sage ruler tolerates me and sets me outside ordinary discipline; where old favor reaches I always receive leniency.
units.literal: Fortunately meeting a sage and enlightened ruler who tolerates me, placing me outside instruction, and moreover where old favor reaches I always receive lenient indulgence.

units.zh: 吾亦自揆疾疹重侵，難復支振，民生安樂之事，心死久矣。
units.en: I also know that rash illness has heavily invaded me and I can hardly hold myself up; the pleasures of life have been dead to my heart for long.
units.literal: I also estimate for myself that rash illness heavily invades and I can hardly support myself again; the affairs of life's ease and joy—my heart has long been dead to them.

units.zh: 所以解日偷存，盡於大布糲粟，半夕安寢，便以自度，血氣盈虛，不復稍道，長以大散為和羹，弟為不見之邪？
units.en: Therefore I steal through my days on coarse cloth and plain grain; half a night's sleep is my measure of well-being; I no longer speak of the ebb and flow of my vitality; I have long taken powdered medicine as my sustenance—do you not see this, younger brother?
units.literal: Therefore I pass days stealing survival, exhausting coarse cloth and coarse grain; half a night's peaceful sleep I take as self-measurement; fullness and emptiness of blood and breath I no longer speak of slightly; long taking great powder as harmonizing broth—do you not see this, younger brother?

units.zh: 疾廢居然，且事一己，上不足敗俗傷化，下不至毀辱家門，泊爾尸居，無方待化。
units.en: Settled in illness and disability, serving only myself—I am not enough to ruin custom above or shame my family below; I dwell like a corpse, awaiting transformation without method.
units.literal: Illness and disability settled thus, and serving only oneself—above not enough to ruin custom and harm transformation, below not reaching to destroy and shame the family gate; placidly like a corpse dwelling, with no method awaiting transformation.

units.zh: 凡此二三，皆是事實。
units.en: All of this is fact.
units.literal: All these two or three are matters of fact.

units.zh: 吾與弟書，不得家中相欺也。
units.en: In writing to you, younger brother, we must not deceive each other within the family.
units.literal: In my letter to you, younger brother, one must not deceive each other within the family.

units.zh: 州陵此舉，為無所因，反覆思之，了不能解。
units.en: Zhouling's action has no cause I can see; thinking it over repeatedly I cannot understand it at all.
units.literal: Zhouling's action in this has no cause whatsoever; thinking it over repeatedly I utterly cannot understand.

units.zh: 豈見吾近者諸牋邪，良可怪笑。
units.en: Did he see my recent letters? That would be truly laughable.
units.literal: Did he see my recent various memorials? Truly something to marvel and laugh at.

units.zh: 吾少學作文，又晚節如小進，使君公欲民不偷，每加存飾，酬對尊貴，不厭敬恭。
units.en: From youth I studied composition, and in later years made some small progress; when lords wished the people not remiss, I always added polish; in answering the great I was never weary of respect.
units.literal: From youth I studied composing writing, and in late years made a small advance; the lord and gentleman wishing the people not to be remiss, each time added preservation and adornment; replying to the honored and noble, never weary of respect and reverence.

units.zh: 且文詞不怨思抑揚，則流澹無味。
units.en: Moreover if literary language lacks modulation of feeling, it flows thin and tasteless.
units.literal: Moreover if literary words lack grievance-thought and modulation, they flow thin and without flavor.

units.zh: 文好古，貴能連類可悲，一往視之，如似多意。
units.en: Writing favors antiquity and values the power to link images into pathos; read through at once it seems full of hidden meaning.
units.literal: Writing favors antiquity, esteeming ability to link categories into what is lamentable; reading through at once it seems to have much meaning.

units.zh: 當見居非求志，清論所排，便是通辭訴屈邪。
units.en: When one sees that one's position is not what one sought and pure discourse rejects it—is that then a general complaint of wrongs?
units.literal: When one sees that dwelling is not seeking one's aim, what pure discourse excludes—is that then general language lodging grievance?

units.zh: 爾者真可謂真素寡矣！
units.en: In that case one may truly be called lacking in plain authenticity!
units.literal: In that case one may truly be called poor in plain authenticity!

units.zh: 其數旦見客小防，自來盈門，亦不煩獨舉吉也。
units.en: I receive visitors only on a few guarded days; they come of themselves filling the gate—I need not trouble to raise auspicious words alone.
units.literal: The number of days I receive guests is small and guarded; they come of themselves filling the gate—I also do not trouble to raise auspicious words alone.

units.zh: 此輩乃云語勢所至，非其要也。
units.en: These people say it is only the momentum of language, not its essence.
units.literal: This crowd then says it is where the momentum of language arrives, not its essentials.

units.zh: 弟無懷居今地，萬物初不以相非，然魯器齊虛，實宜書紳。
units.en: Younger brother, do not be complacent in your present place; all things do not reject each other at first—yet the story of Lu's vessels and Qi's emptiness truly should be written on one's sash.
units.literal: Younger brother, do not harbor dwelling in this place; all things at first do not reject each other—yet Lu vessels and Qi emptiness truly should be written on the sash.

units.zh: 今三署六府之人，誰表裏此內，儻疑弟豫有力，於素論何如哉。
units.en: Among the men of the three offices and six ministries today, who knows the inside and outside of this—if they suspect you had foreknowledge and influence, what of plain discourse?
units.literal: Now among the men of the three offices and six ministries, who inside and outside this—if they suspect younger brother had foreknowledge and power, what of plain discourse?

units.zh: 則吾長阨不死，終誤盛壯也。
units.en: Then I will long linger in obstruction without dying, ultimately misleading my prime years.
units.literal: Then I will long be blocked and not die, ultimately misleading my prime and vigor.

units.zh: 江不過強吹拂吾，云是巖穴人。
units.en: Jiang merely pressed and flattered me, calling me a man of cliff and cave.
units.literal: Jiang merely forcibly blew and brushed me, saying I am a man of cliff and cave.

units.zh: 巖穴人情所高，吾得當此，則雞鶩變作鳳皇，何為干飾廉隅，秩秩見於面目，所惜者大耳。
units.en: Men of cliff and cave are what the world esteems; given this title, chickens and ducks become phoenixes—why bother adorning one's integrity, showing it orderly in one's face? What I regret is the greater matter only.
units.literal: Cliff-and-cave men are what human sentiment esteems; obtaining this, then chickens and ducks change into phoenixes—why bother adorning corner integrity, orderly appearing on the face? What is regretted is great only.

units.zh: 諸舍闔門皆蒙時私，此既未易陳道，故常因含聲不言。
units.en: All our households have received private favor of the time; this is not easy to state, so I often hold my tongue.
units.literal: All the households with closed gates received private favor of the time; this is already not easy to set forth, therefore I often hold sound within and do not speak.

units.zh: 至兄弟，尤為叨竊，臨海頻煩二郡，謙亦越進清階，吾高枕家巷，遂至中書郎，此足以闔棺矣。
units.en: As for my brothers, they have been especially presumptuous—Linhai repeatedly held two commanderies, Qian also rose beyond his station; I with high pillow in my lane reached Palace Gentleman—this is enough to close the coffin.
units.literal: As for brothers, especially presumptuous theft—Linhai repeatedly troubled two commanderies, Qian also overstepped into pure ranks; I with high pillow in the home lane reached Palace Gentleman of the Secretariat—this is enough to close the coffin.

units.zh: 又前年優旨，自弟所宣，雖夏后撫辜人，周宣及鰥寡，不足過也。
units.en: Moreover the favorable edict of two years ago was proclaimed by you; though Yu comforted the guilty and King Xuan of Zhou reached widows and orphans, they could not surpass it.
units.literal: Moreover the favorable edict of the year before last was proclaimed by you, younger brother; though Xia Hou comforted the guilty man and Zhou Xuan reached widowers and widows, it is not enough to surpass this.

units.zh: 語皆循檢校跡，不為虛飾也。
units.en: The words all follow verified facts and are not empty adornment.
units.literal: The words all follow inspected traces and are not empty adornment.

units.zh: 作人不阿諛，無緣頭髮見白，稍學諂詐。
units.en: By nature I do not flatter; without cause for my hair to turn white, I would slightly learn flattery and deceit.
units.literal: Making a man I do not flatter and fawn; without cause for hair to show white, slightly learning flattery and deceit.

units.zh: 且吾何以為，足不能行，自不得出戶；
units.en: Moreover what can I do—my feet cannot walk, so I naturally cannot leave the house;
units.literal: Moreover what can I do—feet cannot walk, naturally cannot go out the door;

units.zh: 頭不耐風，故不可扶曳。
units.en: my head cannot bear wind, so I cannot be supported and led along.
units.literal: the head cannot bear wind, therefore cannot be supported and dragged.

units.zh: 家本貧餧，至於惡衣蔬食，設使盜蹠居此，亦不能兩展其足，妄意珍藏也。
units.en: Our family was originally poor, to the point of coarse clothes and plain food; even Robber Zhi dwelling here could not stretch both feet twice, vainly dreaming of hoarded treasure.
units.literal: The family was originally poor and hungry, to the point of detestable clothes and vegetable food; suppose Robber Zhi dwelt here, he also could not stretch both feet twice, vainly intending treasured store.

units.zh: 正令選官設作此舉，於吾亦無劍戟之傷，所以懃懃畏人之多言也。
units.en: Even if the selection official made this appointment, it would not wound me like sword or halberd; what I earnestly fear is people's gossip.
units.literal: Even if the selection official set up this action, for me there is also no wound of sword and halberd; therefore I earnestly fear people's much talk.

units.zh: 管子晉賢，乃關人主之輕重，此何容易哉。
units.en: Guanzi was a worthy man of Jin, yet concerned the ruler's weight in the balance—how is this easy!
units.literal: Guanzi was Jin's worthy man, yet concerned the ruler's light and heavy—how is this easy!

units.zh: 州陵亦自言視明聽聰，而返區區飾吾，何辯致而下英俊。
units.en: Zhouling also claims clear sight and keen hearing, yet turns to petty flattery of me—what eloquence can bring down outstanding men?
units.literal: Zhouling also himself says he sees clearly and hears keenly, yet returns to petty adorning me—what eloquence to bring down outstanding men.

units.zh: 夫奇士必龍居深藏，與蛙蝦為伍，放勳其猶難之，林宗輩不足識也。
units.en: Extraordinary men must dwell hidden like dragons, keeping company with frogs and shrimp; even Emperor Yao found it hard; men like Guo Linzong are not enough to recognize them.
units.literal: Extraordinary men must like dragons dwell in deep hiding, keeping company with frogs and shrimp; even Fangxun still found it hard; Lin Zong's sort are not enough to recognize them.

units.zh: 似不肯睠睠奉牋記，雕琢獻文章，居家近市廛，親戚滿城府，吾猶自知袁陽源輩當平此不？
units.en: Seemingly unwilling to present polished memorials and carved compositions, dwelling near the market with kin filling the city offices—I still know whether men like Yuan Yangyuan would approve of this, do I not?
units.literal: Seemingly unwilling attentively to present memorials, carving and polishing to offer literary compositions, dwelling near market stalls, kin filling city offices—I still know myself whether Yuan Yangyuan's sort ought to level this or not?

units.zh: 飾詐之與直獨，兩不關吾心，又何所耿介。
units.en: Adorning deceit and plain solitude—neither concerns my heart; what is there to be indignant about?
units.literal: Adorning deceit and plain solitude—neither concerns my heart; what is there to be upright and aloof about?

units.zh: 弟自宜以解塞群賢矣，兼悉怒此言自爾家任兄故能也。
units.en: Younger brother, you yourself ought to use this to answer the worthy men; moreover I fully know that anger at these words comes from your Elder Brother Ren's influence.
units.literal: Younger brother, you yourself ought to use this to answer and block the crowd of worthies; moreover I fully know anger at these words comes from your family's Elder Brother Ren's ability.

units.zh: 日日望弟來，屬病終不起，何意向與江書，粗布胸心，無人可寫，比面乃具與弟。
units.en: Day by day I hoped you would come; illness kept me from rising; I had intended the letter to Jiang to spread my heart roughly, with no one to write it—only now face to face do I give it fully to you.
units.literal: Day by day I hoped you would come; entrusted with illness I ultimately could not rise; my intent was toward the letter to Jiang, roughly spreading the breast's core; no one to write—only now face to face do I fully give it to you, younger brother.

units.zh: 書便覺成，本以當半日相見，吾既惡勞，不得多語，樞機幸非所長，相見亦不勝讀此書也。
units.en: The letter then seemed complete; I had thought we would meet half a day—I hate exertion and cannot speak much; statecraft is fortunately not my strength; meeting face to face also cannot match reading this letter.
units.literal: The letter then seemed complete; originally I thought we would meet half a day—I already hate labor and cannot speak much; pivot and trigger fortunately are not my strength; meeting face to face also cannot surpass reading this letter.

units.zh: 親屬欲見自可示，無急付手。
units.en: If kin wish to see it you may show them; no need to hand it over in haste.
units.literal: If kin wish to see it you may show it yourself; no need urgently to put it in hand.

units.zh: 時論者或云微之見舉，廬江何偃亦豫其議，慮為微所咎，與書自陳。
units.en: Some said that when Wei was recommended, He Yan of Lujiang also took part in the deliberation; fearing blame from Wei, he wrote to explain himself.
units.literal: At the time some in discussion said that in Wei's being recommended, He Yan of Lujiang also took part in the deliberation; fearing blame from Wei, he wrote a letter explaining himself.

units.zh: 微報之曰：
units.en: Wei replied:
units.literal: Wei replied saying:

units.zh: 卿昔稱吾於義興，吾常謂之見知，然復自怪鄙野，不參風流，未有一介熟悉於事，何用獨識之也。
units.en: You once praised me at Yixing; I took that for true recognition, yet I marvel at my own rustic nature—I never joined the elegant world, had no friend familiar with affairs—why single me out?
units.literal: You once praised me at Yixing; I always called that being known; yet again I wonder at my own rustic wildness, not joining the current of elegance, not having one acquaintance familiar with affairs—what use to know me alone?

units.zh: 近日何見綽送卿書，雖知如戲，知卿固不能相哀。
units.en: Recently I saw Chuo deliver your letter; though I know it was in jest, I know you truly cannot pity me.
units.literal: Recently He Jianchuo sent your letter; though I know it as jest, I know you solidly cannot pity me.

units.zh: 苟相哀之未知，何相期之可論。
units.en: If pity between us is not yet known, what expectation can be discussed?
units.literal: If mutual pity is not yet known, what mutual expectation can be discussed?

units.zh: 卿少陶玄風，淹雅脩暢，自是正始中人。
units.en: From youth you were steeped in metaphysical discourse, refined and fluent—naturally a man of the Zhengshi era.
units.literal: From youth you were steeped in arcane wind, steeped in elegance and cultivated fluency—naturally a man of the Zhengshi era.

units.zh: 吾真庸性人耳，自然志操不倍王、樂。
units.en: I am truly a commonplace man; by nature my aims do not match those of Wang Bi and Yue Guang.
units.literal: I am truly a man of common nature only; by nature my aim and conduct do not double Wang and Yue.

units.zh: 小兒時尤麤笨無好，常從博士讀小小章句，竟無可得，口吃不能劇讀，遂絕意於尋求。
units.en: In childhood I was especially coarse and dull, often reading small passages with tutors but gaining nothing; I stammered and could not read aloud, and gave up serious study.
units.literal: In childhood especially coarse, clumsy, and without excellence, I often followed the erudite reading small passages and sentences, ultimately obtaining nothing; stammering I could not read intensely, and therefore cut off intent in seeking.

units.zh: 至二十左右，方復就觀小說，往來者見床頭有數帙書，便言學問，試就檢，當何有哉。
units.en: Only around twenty did I read minor fiction again; visitors seeing books by my bed would speak of learning—inspect them and what would you find?
units.literal: Only around twenty did I again approach reading minor fiction; visitors seeing several fascicles of books at the bed head would speak of learning—try inspecting, what would there be?

units.zh: 乃復持此擬議人邪。
units.en: Yet you use this to judge men?
units.literal: Yet you again use this to judge and discuss men?

units.zh: 尚獨愧咲揚子之褒贍，猶恥辭賦為君子，若吾篆刻，菲亦甚矣。
units.en: I still blush to laugh at Yang Xiong's generous praise and still find rhapsodies unworthy of a gentleman—how much more slight is my seal carving.
units.literal: I still alone feel ashamed to laugh at Yangzi's generous praise, still ashamed of rhapsodies and fu as gentlemanly—if my seal carving, how very slight also.

units.zh: 卿諸人亦當尤以此見議。
units.en: You gentlemen also ought especially to be criticized on this account.
units.literal: You gentlemen also ought especially to be criticized for this.

units.zh: 或謂言深博，作一段意氣，鄙薄人世，初不敢然。
units.en: Some say my words are profound, making a show of spirit and despising the world—I never dared do so.
units.literal: Some say my words are deep and broad, making a stretch of spirit and energy, despising and slighting the human world—I at first did not dare so.

units.zh: 是以每見世人文賦書論，無所是非，不解處即日借問，此其本心也。
units.en: Therefore whenever I see the world's essays and treatises I pass no judgment; where I do not understand I ask at once—that is my true heart.
units.literal: Therefore whenever I see the world's literary fu, books, and disquisitions, I have no right or wrong; where I do not understand I borrow and ask the same day—this is my original heart.

units.zh: 至於生平好服上藥，起年十二時病虛耳。
units.en: As for my lifelong fondness for superior medicines, it began when at twelve I suffered from deficiency illness.
units.literal: As for loving superior drugs throughout life, it began when at twelve I was ill with deficiency only.

units.zh: 所撰服食方中，粗言之矣。
units.en: I have spoken of it roughly in the ingestion formulas I compiled.
units.literal: In the ingestion formulas I compiled I have spoken of it roughly.

units.zh: 自此始信攝養有徵，故門冬昌朮，隨時參進。
units.en: From this I began to believe regulated nourishment has effect; therefore I take ophiopogon and atractylodes according to the season.
units.literal: From this I began to believe nurturing regulation has evidence; therefore ophiopogon and atractylodes I add according to the season.

units.zh: 寒溫相補，欲以扶護危羸，見冀白首。
units.en: Balancing cold and warm properties, I wish thereby to sustain my frail body and hope to reach old age.
units.literal: Cold and warm mutually supplementing, wishing thereby to support and protect the perilously frail, hoping to see white head.

units.zh: 家貧乏役，至於春秋令節，輒自將兩三門生，入草采之。
units.en: Our family was poor and lacked servants; at spring and autumn festivals I would myself lead two or three students into the fields to gather herbs.
units.literal: The family was poor and lacked servants; at spring and autumn festival seasons I would myself lead two or three students into the grasses to gather them.

units.zh: 吾實倦遊醫部，頗曉和藥，尤信《本草》，欲其必行，是以躬親，意在取精。
units.en: I have grown weary of medical offices, understand compounding fairly well, and especially trust the Materia Medica; wishing remedies to be effective, I gather herbs myself to obtain the finest.
units.literal: I truly am weary of wandering the medical departments, quite understand compounding drugs, especially trust the Materia Medica, wishing it must be effective—therefore personally attend, intent on taking the refined.

units.zh: 世人便言希仙好異，矯慕不羈，不同家頗有罵之者。
units.en: The world then says I seek immortality and love the strange, pretentiously admiring untrammeled ways—even within my family some revile this.
units.literal: The world then says I hope for immortals and love the strange, pretentiously admiring untrammeled license—within the family there are quite a few who revile this.

units.zh: 又性知畫繢，蓋亦鳴鵠識夜之機，盤紆糾紛，或記心目，故兼山水之愛，一往跡求，皆仿像也。
units.en: Moreover I know painting by nature—perhaps like the goose that knows night by its call; winding forms sometimes fixed in the mind's eye; therefore I also love landscape; whenever I go to trace them, all are likenesses.
units.literal: Moreover by nature I know painting and ornament—perhaps also the mechanism by which the calling goose knows night; winding and tangled confusion, sometimes recorded in eye and mind; therefore combined love of mountains and waters; going once to trace and seek, all are likenesses.

units.zh: 不好詣人，能忘榮以避權右，宜自密應對舉止，因卷慙自保，不能勉其所短耳。
units.en: I do not like calling on people and can forget glory to avoid the powerful; one ought to be reserved in speech and bearing; I curl inward in shame to preserve myself and cannot force what is beyond my strength.
units.literal: I do not like calling on people, can forget glory to avoid the powerful on the right; one ought oneself to be secret in response and deportment, therefore curling in shame to preserve myself—cannot force what is my shortcoming only.

units.zh: 由來有此數條，二三諸賢，因復架累，致之高塵，詠之清壑。
units.en: These traits have long existed; two or three worthies piled reputation upon them, raising them to lofty heights and chanting them in clear valleys.
units.literal: From of old there have been these several items; two or three worthies again piled frames upon them, raising them to high dust, chanting them in clear ravines.

units.zh: 瓦礫有資，不敢輕廁金銀也。
units.en: Tiles and rubble have their place—I dare not lightly rank them with gold and silver.
units.literal: Tiles and rubble have their use—I dare not lightly mix them with gold and silver.

units.zh: 而頃年嬰疾，沉淪無已，區區之情，愒於生存，自恐難復，而先命猥加，魂氣褰薾，常人不得作常自處疾苦，正亦臥思已熟，謂有記自論。
units.en: Yet in recent years illness has held me in endless decline; my petty heart is weary of living and I fear I cannot recover—yet fate has been prematurely imposed, my spirit drooping; ordinary men cannot constantly dwell amid illness; lying abed I have thought it through and believe there is matter for self-account.
units.literal: Yet in recent years I have been afflicted with illness, sinking without end; my petty feelings are weary of survival, myself fearing hard recovery—yet life prematurely added, soul and breath drooping and withering; ordinary men cannot constantly place themselves amid illness; lying down I have also thought it through and believe there is record for self-discussion.

units.zh: 既仰天光，不夭庶類，兼望諸賢，共相哀體，而卿首唱誕言，布之翰墨，萬石之慎，或未然邪。
units.en: Having looked up to Heaven's light and hoped not to cut life short, I also hoped the worthies would pity me together—yet you first raised extravagant words and spread them in writing; the caution of a man of ten thousand piculs—perhaps that is not so?
units.literal: Having looked up to Heaven's light, not cutting short the multitude, I also hoped the worthies would together pity my person—yet you first raised extravagant words and spread them in brush and ink; the caution of ten thousand piculs—perhaps it is not so?

units.zh: 好盡之累，豈其如此。
units.en: The burden of saying all one thinks—can it be thus?
units.literal: The burden of loving to exhaust all—can it be thus?

units.zh: 綽大駭歎，便是闔朝見病者。
units.en: Jianchuo was greatly startled and sighed—then the whole court will see the sick man.
units.literal: Jianchuo greatly startled and sighed—then it is the whole court seeing the ill man.

units.zh: 吾本儜人，加疹意惛，一旦聞此，便惶怖矣。
units.en: I am by nature a weak man, and with rash illness my mind is dim; hearing this at once I was terrified.
units.literal: I am originally a weak man, added rash making mind dim; once hearing this I was at once fearful and terrified.

units.zh: 五六日來，復苦心痛，引喉狀如胸中悉腫，甚自憂。
units.en: For five or six days I have again suffered heart pain, with a constricted throat as if my chest were entirely swollen—I am deeply worried.
units.literal: For five or six days now again bitter heart pain, drawing the throat as if the chest were entirely swollen—greatly worried myself.

units.zh: 力作此答，無復條貫，貴布所懷，落漠不舉。
units.en: I force myself to write this reply without order or coherence, valuing only to spread what is in my heart, desolate and unable to rise.
units.literal: Forcing myself to make this reply, no longer with order and thread; valuing spreading what is in the breast, desolate and not raised.

units.zh: 卿既不可解，立欲便別，且當笑。
units.en: Since you cannot understand, you wish at once to part—we may only laugh.
units.literal: Since you cannot understand, you immediately wish to part—one may only laugh.

units.zh: 微常住門屋一間，尋書玩古，如此者十餘年。
units.en: Wei lived constantly in a single gate-house room, seeking books and enjoying antiquities—for more than ten years.
units.literal: Wei constantly dwelt in one room of the gate house, seeking books and enjoying antiquities—thus for more than ten years.

units.zh: 太祖以其善筮，賜以名蓍。
units.en: Taizu, because he was skilled at divination, bestowed famous yarrow stalks on him.
units.literal: Taizu because he was skilled at divination bestowed famous yarrow stalks on him.

units.zh: 弟僧謙，亦有才譽，為太子舍人，遇疾，微躬自處治，而僧謙服藥失度，遂卒。
units.en: His younger brother Sengqian also had talent and reputation and served as Attendant in the Heir Apparent's household; when he fell ill Wei treated him personally, but Sengqian took medicine in excess and died.
units.literal: Younger brother Sengqian also had talent and reputation, served as Attendant in the Heir Apparent's household; encountering illness, Wei personally attended treatment, yet Sengqian took medicine beyond measure and thus died.

units.zh: 微深自咎恨，發病不復自治，哀痛僧謙不能已，以書告靈曰：
units.en: Wei blamed himself deeply, fell ill and no longer treated himself, and could not cease grieving for Sengqian; he wrote to tell the spirit:
units.literal: Wei deeply blamed himself, fell ill and no longer treated himself, grief for Sengqian could not cease, and with a letter he told the spirit saying:

units.zh: 弟年十五，始居宿於外，不為察慧之譽，獨沉浮好書，聆琴聞操，輒有過目之能。
units.en: My brother at fifteen first lodged away from home, without a reputation for keen wisdom, devoted only to books; hearing the zither or a melody, he retained it at a glance.
units.literal: Younger brother at fifteen first lodged and slept outside, without reputation for keen wisdom, alone drifting in love of books; hearing zither and listening to pieces, he always had ability to pass the eyes.

units.zh: 討測文典，斟酌傳記，寒暑未交，便卓然可述。
units.en: Probing the classics and weighing biographies, before a year had passed he was already outstandingly accomplished.
units.literal: Investigating and measuring literary canons, weighing biographies and records, cold and heat not yet exchanged, he was already outstandingly worth recounting.

units.zh: 吾長病，或有小間，輒稱引前載，不異舊學。
units.en: I was long ill; when I had a brief respite he would cite former records no differently from a seasoned scholar.
units.literal: I was long ill; when there was a small respite he would cite and draw on former records, no different from old learning.

units.zh: 自爾日就月將，著名邦黨，方隆夙志，嗣美前賢，何圖一旦冥然長往，酷痛煩冤，心如焚裂。
units.en: From then he advanced day by day, famed in our district, just then fulfilling his long-cherished aims and succeeding the beauty of former worthies—who dreamed that one morning he would depart into darkness? Bitter pain and vexing grief—my heart feels burned and torn.
units.literal: From then day by day advancing, month by month progressing, famed in the district and clique, just then raising long-cherished aim, succeeding the beauty of former worthies—who planned that in one morning he would dimly make the long journey? Bitter pain and vexing wrong, heart like burning and splitting.

units.zh: 尋念平生，裁十年中耳。
units.en: Looking back on our life together—it is only ten years in all.
units.literal: Searching my thoughts through life—it is only ten years in all.

units.zh: 然非公事，無不相對，一字之書，必共詠讀；
units.en: Yet unless it was public business we were never apart; a single character's worth of writing we would chant and read together;
units.literal: Yet unless it was public business, there was nothing we did not face together; a book of one character we must chant and read together;

units.zh: 一句之文，無不研賞，濁酒忘愁，圖籍相慰，吾所以窮而不憂，實賴此耳。
units.en: a single sentence of prose we would study and admire; muddy wine to forget sorrow, books to comfort each other—the reason I was poor yet untroubled truly lay in this.
units.literal: a text of one sentence, none we did not study and admire; muddy wine forgetting sorrow, maps and records comforting each other—why I was poor yet not worried truly relied on this.

units.zh: 奈何罪酷，煢然獨坐。
units.en: Alas for cruel fate—I sit alone and orphaned.
units.literal: Alas for cruel fate—I sit alone and orphaned.

units.zh: 憶往年散發，極目流涕，吾不舍日夜，又恆慮吾羸病，豈圖奄忽，先歸冥冥。
units.en: I recall former years with hair unbound, gazing far with streaming tears—I never left him day or night, always worrying over my frail illness—who dreamed he would suddenly depart first into the darkness?
units.literal: Recalling former years with hair unbound, gazing to the limit with streaming tears—I did not leave day or night, and always worried over my frail illness—who planned sudden departure, returning first to the dark dark?

units.zh: 反覆萬慮，無復一期，音顏髣髴，觸事歷然，弟今何在，令吾悲窮。
units.en: Turning over ten thousand thoughts, we shall meet no more; his voice and face seem present, every matter vividly clear—where is my brother now, driving my grief to the limit.
units.literal: Turning over ten thousand thoughts, no more one meeting; voice and face seeming there, touching affairs vividly clear—where is younger brother now, making my grief extreme.

units.zh: 昔仕京師，分張六旬耳，其中三過，誤云今日何意不來，鍾念懸心，無物能譬。
units.en: When I served the capital we were apart only sixty days; within that time three times he mistakenly asked why I had not come that day—such concentrated longing, nothing can compare.
units.literal: Formerly serving the capital, we were apart only sixty days in all; within that three times he mistakenly said why do you not come today—concentrated thought suspended heart, nothing can compare.

units.zh: 方欲共營林澤，以送餘年，念茲有何罪戾，見此夭酷，沒於吾手，觸事痛恨。
units.en: We were just about to retire together to woods and streams to spend our remaining years—what crime is this, to see such untimely cruelty and that he perished by my hand—at every turn I hate bitterly.
units.literal: We were just about to together manage woods and marshes to send off remaining years—thinking on this what crime or fault, seeing this untimely cruelty, perishing in my hands—touching affairs I hate bitterly.

units.zh: 吾素好醫術，不使弟子得全，又尋思不精，致有枉過，念此一條，特復痛酷。
units.en: I have long loved medicine yet did not preserve my disciple; reflecting that my skill was not refined and caused a wrongful death—on this account especially I grieve bitterly.
units.literal: I have long loved medical arts yet did not let my disciple attain wholeness; again reflecting that my thought was not refined, causing wrongful passing—thinking on this one item, especially again bitter pain.

units.zh: 痛酷奈何！
units.en: Bitter pain—what can be done!
units.literal: Bitter pain—what can be done!

units.zh: 吾罪奈何！
units.en: My guilt—what can be done!
units.literal: My guilt—what can be done!

units.zh: 弟為志，奉親孝，事兄順，雖僮僕無所叱咄，可謂君子不失色于人，不失口於人。
units.en: In conduct my brother served his parents filially and his elder brother obediently; he never scolded even servants—truly a gentleman who never lost composure or spoke harshly to others.
units.literal: Younger brother in conduct: serving parents filially, serving elder brother obediently; though servants and slaves he never rebuked or scolded—one may say a gentleman who does not lose color before others, does not lose words before others.

units.zh: 沖和淹通，內有皁白，舉動尺寸，吾每咨之。
units.en: Mild and penetrating, inwardly discerning right from wrong—in every movement's measure I always consulted him.
units.literal: Mild and harmonious, steeped and penetrating, inwardly possessing black and white; in every movement's measure I always consulted him.

units.zh: 常云：「兄文骨氣，可推英麗以自許。
units.en: He often said, "Brother, your writing has true bone and spirit—you may claim heroic beauty for yourself.
units.literal: He often said: "Elder brother's literary bone and breath can be extended to heroic beauty for self-commendation.

units.zh: 又兄為人矯介欲過，宜每中和。」
units.en: Again, brother, you are upright and exacting almost to excess—you ought always to seek the mean."
units.literal: Again elder brother as a man is upright and exacting almost to excess—you ought each time to harmonize the center."

units.zh: 道此猶在耳，萬世不復一見，奈何！
units.en: These words are still in my ears—never in ten thousand generations shall I see him again—what can be done!
units.literal: These words are still in the ear—ten thousand generations will not see him once again—what can be done!

units.zh: 唯十紙手跡，封拆儼然，至於思戀不可懷。
units.en: Only ten sheets in his hand remain, sealed and opened as if yesterday—as for longing, it cannot be borne in the heart.
units.literal: Only ten sheets of handwriting, sealed and opened still intact—as for longing and remembrance, it cannot be held in the breast.

units.zh: 及聞吾病，肝心寸絕，謂當以幅巾薄葬之事累汝，奈何反相殯送！
units.en: When he heard I was ill his heart broke inch by inch; he said he would burden you with arranging a simple burial in plain cloth—how could it be that instead you bore him to the grave!
units.literal: When he heard of my illness his liver and heart broke inch by inch; he said he would burden you with the matter of headcloth and simple burial—how could it be that instead you bore each other in funeral escort!

units.zh: 弟由來意謂：「婦人雖無子，不宜踐二庭。
units.en: Brother had long held that "though a woman has no son, she ought not enter a second household.
units.literal: Younger brother from of old meant: "Though a woman has no son, she ought not tread two courts.

units.zh: 此風若行，便可家有孝婦」。
units.en: If this custom prevailed, every house could have a filial wife."
units.literal: If this wind is practiced, then every house can have a filial wife."

units.zh: 仲長《昌言》，亦其大要。
units.en: Zhongchang Tong's Open Words also states the same essentials.
units.literal: Zhongchang's Open Words also states its great essentials.

units.zh: 劉新婦以刑傷自誓，必留供養；
units.en: Liu the new wife vowed by self-injury to remain and provide for the household;
units.literal: Liu the new wife by cutting and wounding vowed herself, surely to remain for provision;

units.zh: 殷太妃感柏舟之節，不奪其志。
units.en: Grand Consort Yin, moved by the integrity of Cypress Boat, did not override her resolve.
units.literal: Lady Yin the Grand Consort, moved by the integrity of Cypress Boat, did not wrest away her resolve.

units.zh: 僕射篤順，范夫人知禮，求得左率第五兒，廬位有主。
units.en: The Vice Director was sincere and obedient, Lady Fan knew ritual; they sought the fifth son of the Left Commander—the mourning place had its master.
units.literal: The Vice Director was sincere and obedient, Lady Fan knew ritual; they sought the fifth son of the Left Commander—the mourning hut had a master.

units.zh: 此亦何益冥然之痛，為是存者意耳。
units.en: This also does nothing for pain in the darkness—it is only the wish of those who remain.
units.literal: This also what use for dark pain—it is only the intent of those who remain.

units.zh: 吾窮疾之人，平生意志，弟實知之。
units.en: I, a man broken by illness—my lifelong intent my brother truly knew.
units.literal: I, a man exhausted by illness—my lifelong intent younger brother truly knew.

units.zh: 端坐向窗，有何慰適，正賴弟耳。
units.en: Sitting upright by the window, what comfort is there—I truly relied on my brother alone.
units.literal: Sitting upright facing the window, what comfort and ease—truly relying on younger brother only.

units.zh: 過中未來，已自愒望，今云何得立，自省惛毒，無復人理。
units.en: Past noon he did not come and I was already weary with waiting; now how can I stand? Reflecting on myself in dim anguish—I am no longer human.
units.literal: Past noon he did not come—I was already weary with longing; now how can I stand? Examining myself in dim anguish—I am no longer within human norms.

units.zh: 比煩冤困憊，不能作刻石文，若靈響有識，不得吾文，豈不為恨。
units.en: Lately vexed and exhausted, I cannot compose an inscription; if your spirit has awareness and does not receive my words, would that not be regret?
units.literal: Lately vexed, wronged, exhausted and weary, unable to make inscribed stone text—if the spirit's echo has awareness and does not receive my text, would it not be regret?

units.zh: 儻意慮不遂，謝能思之如狂，不知所告訴，明書此數紙，無復詞理，略道阡陌，萬不寫一。
units.en: If my thoughts cannot be fulfilled, Xie can think of it like madness, not knowing whom to tell; plainly writing these sheets without order or reason, briefly tracing our paths—of ten thousand things not one is written.
units.literal: If intent and thought are not fulfilled, Xie can think of it like madness, not knowing whom to tell; clearly writing these several sheets, no more words and reason, briefly telling paths between fields—ten thousand not written one.

units.zh: 阿謙！
units.en: Ah, Qian!
units.literal: Ah, Qian!

units.zh: 何圖至此！
units.en: Who dreamed it would come to this!
units.literal: Who planned it would come to this!

units.zh: 誰復視我，誰復憂我！
units.en: Who will look upon me again, who will care for me again!
units.literal: Who again will regard me, who again will worry for me!

units.zh: 他日寶惜三光，割嗜好以祈年，今也唯速化耳。
units.en: Other days I treasured sun, moon, and stars and gave up pleasures to pray for long life—now I wish only swift dissolution.
units.literal: Other days I treasured the three lights, cut off preferences to pray for years—now only swift transformation.

units.zh: 吾豈復支，冥冥中竟復云何。
units.en: How can I go on—in the darkness what will become of us?
units.literal: How can I again support myself—in the dark dark what again will it be?

units.zh: 弟懷隨、和之寶，未及光諸文章，欲收作一集，不知忽忽當辦此不？
