units.en: Brother held treasures like those of Sui and He, not yet brought to light in writing; I wished to gather his works into one collection—will it be done in time?
units.literal: Younger brother held the treasures of Sui and He, not yet reaching to illumine the various writings; I wished to gather them into one collection—do you know whether in haste this can be done?

units.zh: 今已成服，吾臨靈取常共飲杯，酌自釀酒，寧有仿像不？
units.en: Now in mourning dress, I approach the spirit and take the cup we often shared, pour wine I brewed myself—is there perhaps some likeness of you?
units.literal: Now mourning garments are complete; I approach the spirit and take the cup we often drank together, pour self-brewed wine—is there perhaps some likeness?

units.zh: 冤痛！
units.en: Wronged pain!
units.literal: Wronged pain!

units.zh: 冤痛！
units.en: Wronged pain!
units.literal: Wronged pain!

units.zh: 元嘉三十年，卒，時年三十九。
units.en: He died in the thirtieth year of Yuanjia, at the age of thirty-nine.
units.literal: In the thirtieth year of Yuanjia he died, aged thirty-nine.

units.zh: 僧謙卒後四旬而微終。
units.en: Wei died forty days after Sengqian.
units.literal: Forty days after Sengqian's death Wei ended.

units.zh: 遺令薄葬，不設轜旐鼓挽之屬，施五尺床，為靈二宿便毀。
units.en: His final instructions were for a simple burial, without funeral carts, banners, drums, or processions; provide a five-foot couch; after two nights before the spirit, destroy it.
units.literal: His final command was simple burial, not setting out funeral carts, banners, drums, or pulling teams; provide a five-foot couch; after two nights at the spirit, destroy it.

units.zh: 以嘗所彈琴置床上，何長史來，以琴與之。
units.en: Place the zither he once played on the couch; when Chief Clerk He comes, give him the zither.
units.literal: Place the zither he once played on the couch; when Chief Clerk He comes, give him the zither.

units.zh: 何長史者，偃也。
units.en: Chief Clerk He was He Yan.
units.literal: Chief Clerk He was Yan.

units.zh: 無子。
units.en: He left no sons.
units.literal: He had no sons.

units.zh: 家人遵之。
units.en: The family followed his instructions.
units.literal: The family followed this.

units.zh: 所著文集傳於世。
units.en: His collected writings circulated in the world.
units.literal: The collected writings he authored were transmitted in the world.

units.zh: 世祖即位，詔曰：「微棲志貞深，文行惇洽，生自華宗，身安隱素，足以賁茲丘園，惇是薄俗。
units.en: When Emperor Shizu ascended the throne, an edict read: "Wei dwelt with pure and deep intent, his literary conduct sincere and harmonious; born of a great clan, he lived at ease in plain simplicity—enough to adorn these hills and gardens and enrich this shallow age.
units.literal: When Shizu took the throne an edict said: "Wei dwelt with intent pure and deep, literary conduct sincere and harmonious, born from a splendid clan, personally at ease in plain simplicity—enough to adorn these hills and gardens and thicken this thin custom.

units.zh: 不幸蚤世，朕甚悼之。
units.en: He died untimely, and I deeply mourn him.
units.literal: Unfortunate early death—I deeply mourn him.

units.zh: 可追贈秘書監。」
units.en: Let him be posthumously awarded Director of the Secretariat."
units.literal: He may be posthumously awarded Director of the Secretariat."

units.zh: 史臣曰：燕太子吐一言，田先生吞舌而死；
units.en: The historiographer says: The Crown Prince of Yan spoke one word, and Master Tian swallowed his tongue and died;
units.literal: The historiographer says: The Crown Prince of Yan spoke one word and Master Tian swallowed his tongue and died;

units.zh: 安邑令戒屠者，閔仲叔去而之沛。
units.en: the magistrate of Anyi warned the butcher, and Min Zhongshu left for Pei.
units.literal: the magistrate of Anyi warned the butcher, and Min Zhongshu left and went to Pei.

units.zh: 良由內懷耿介，峻節不可輕干。
units.en: Truly because inwardly they harbor upright integrity—lofty integrity cannot be lightly offended.
units.literal: Truly because inwardly they harbor upright integrity—lofty integrity cannot be lightly offended.

units.zh: 袁淑笑謔之間，而王微弔詞連牘，斯蓋好名之士，欲以身為珪璋，皦皦然使塵玷之累，不能加也。
units.en: Between Yuan Shu's laughter and jest, Wang Wei produced condolence letters sheet after sheet—such men love fame and wish to make themselves jade regalia, bright and clear so that the stain of dust cannot touch them.
units.literal: Between Yuan Shu's laughter and jest, Wang Wei's condolence words linked sheets—this is probably a man who loves fame, wishing to make his person jade regalia, bright and clear so that the burden of dust and stain cannot be added.

units.zh: 帝中康時，羲、和湎淫，廢時亂日。
units.en: Under Zhongkang the Xi and He stewards sank into vice and threw the calendar into confusion.
units.literal: Emperor Zhongkang's time, Xi and He drowned in debauchery, abandoned seasons disordered days.

units.zh: 禹之父曰鯀，鯀之父曰帝顓頊，顓頊之父曰昌意，昌意之父曰黃帝。
units.en: Yu's father was Gun; Gun's father was Emperor Zhuanxu; Zhuanxu's father was Changyi; Changyi's father was the Yellow Emperor.
units.literal: Yu's father was called Gun; Gun's father was called Emperor Zhuanxu; Zhuanxu's father was called Changyi; Changyi's father was the Yellow Emperor.

units.zh: 領軍將軍謝晦謂延之曰：「昔荀勗忌阮咸，斥為始平郡，今卿又為始安，可謂二始。」
units.en: Xie Hui, General-in-Chief, told him: "Long ago Xun Xu envied Ruan Xian and sent him off to Shiping; now you are posted to Shi'an—you might call it a pair of 'Shi' banishments."
units.literal: General-in-Chief Xie Hui said to Yanzhi: "In the past Xun Xu resented Ruan Xian and banished him to Shiping commandery; now you are again made Administrator of Shi'an—this may be called the two Shi's."

units.zh: 詠阮咸曰：「屢薦不入官，一麾乃出守。」
units.en: Of Ruan Xian: "Recommended again and again, yet never given office—a single gesture, and he is sent to rule a province."
units.literal: On Ruan Xian: "Repeatedly recommended yet not entering office; one wave of the hand and he is sent out to govern."

units.zh: 漢末仲長統謂百司皆宜執之。
units.en: Late in Han, Zhongchang Tong argued that every office should carry them.
units.literal: At the end of Han, Zhongchang Tong said all offices should hold them.

units.zh: 自斯以後，晉道彌昏，道子開其禍端，元顯成其末釁，桓玄藉運乘時，加以先父之業，因基革命，人無異心。
units.en: From then on Jin's way grew ever darker; Daozi opened the source of calamity and Yuanxian completed the final provocation; Huan Xuan rode fortune and seized the season, adding his father's former enterprise, and thereby founded revolution—among the people there was no divergent heart.
units.literal: From then on Jin's way grew ever darker; Daozi opened the source of calamity and Yuanxian completed the final provocation; Huan Xuan rode fortune and seized the season, adding his father's former enterprise, and thereby founded revolution—among the people there was no divergent heart.

units.zh: 對捍使者尚得死坐，況遊道吐不臣之言，犯慢上之罪，口稱夷、齊，心懷盜跖，欺公賣法，受納苞苴，產隨官厚，財與位積，雖贓汚未露，而姦詐如是。
units.en: Resisting an envoy earns death; how much more unministered words, slighting superiors, mouth naming Yi and Qi while heart harbors robbers, deceiving the public, taking bribes—wealth piled with rank though bribery was not yet exposed.
units.literal: Resisting an envoy still earns death; how much more Youdao's unministered words, the crime of slighting superiors, mouth naming Yi and Qi while heart harboring robbers, deceiving the public and selling the law, receiving wrapped bribes—property following office thick, wealth with rank piled; though bribery was not yet exposed, treachery was such.

units.zh: 循既走還廣州，恩又領千餘人隨劉藩追徐道覆於始興，斬之。
units.en: After Xun fled back to Guangzhou, En led more than a thousand men under Liu Fan to pursue Xu Daofu at Shixing and killed him.
units.literal: After Xun had fled back to Guangzhou, En again led more than a thousand men following Liu Fan to pursue Xu Daofu at Shixing and beheaded him.

units.zh: 又隨劉藩追徐道覆於始興，斬之。
units.en: He again followed Liu Fan to pursue Xu Daofu at Shixing and killed him.
units.literal: He again followed Liu Fan to pursue Xu Daofu at Shixing and beheaded him.

units.zh: 復隨劉藩至始興，討斬徐道覆。
units.en: He again followed Liu Fan to Shixing, where Xu Daofu was hunted down and killed.
units.literal: He again followed Liu Fan to Shixing and attacked and beheaded Xu Daofu.

units.zh: 孝武時，侍中何偃南郊陪乘，鑾輅過白門閫，偃將匐，帝乃接之曰：「朕乃陪卿。」
units.en: Under Emperor Xiaowu, He Yan, gentleman-in-attendance, rode beside the emperor at the southern suburb; as the train passed the White Gate barbican he was about to bow flat, and the emperor stayed him: "I shall keep you company."
units.literal: In the Xiaowu era the gentleman-in-attendance He Yan rode beside the emperor at the southern suburb; when the imperial carriage passed the White Gate barbican Yan was about to prostrate himself, and the emperor caught him up, saying, "I shall accompany you."

units.zh: 國相孔融深敬於玄，履履造門。
units.en: State chancellor Kong Rong revered him deeply and hurried to his door in his house slippers.
units.literal: The state chancellor Kong Rong deeply revered Xuan and, treading his slippers, went to his gate.

units.zh: 告高密縣為玄特立一鄉，曰：『昔齊置「土鄉」，越有「君子軍」，皆異賢之意也。
units.en: He told Gaomi county to carve out a special township, saying: "Qi once founded a 'scholar township' and Yue a 'gentlemen's host'—both honored worthies.
units.literal: He instructed Gaomi county to establish a separate township for Xuan, saying: 'Formerly Qi set up a "scholar township" and Yue had a "gentlemen's army"—all expressing esteem for the worthy.

units.zh: 今鄭君鄉宜曰「鄭公鄉」。
units.en: Master Zheng's township should therefore be named the Township of Lord Zheng."
units.literal: Now Lord Zheng's township ought to be called "Lord Zheng township."

units.zh: 可廣開門衢，令容高車，號為「通德門」。』
units.en: Widen the lanes and gates for high-wheeled carriages and call the approach the Gate of Pervading Virtue."
units.literal: You may widen the thoroughfare and gates to admit tall carts, and style it the Gate of Pervading Virtue.'

units.zh: 鄭君好學，實懷明德。
units.en: Master Zheng loves learning and bears shining virtue.
units.literal: Lord Zheng loves learning and truly harbors bright virtue.

units.zh: 昔太史公、廷尉吳公、謁者仆射鄧公，皆漢之名臣。
units.en: In the past, the Grand Historian, Commandant of Justice Wu, and Supervisor of the Internuncio Deng were all famous ministers of Han.
units.literal: Formerly the grand scribe, minister of trials Wu, and chief herald Deng were all famous ministers of Han.

units.zh: 又南山四皓有園公、夏黃公，潛光隱耀，世嘉其高，皆悉稱公。
units.en: Among the South Mountain Four, Lord Yuan and Lord Xia Huang hid their light; the world praised their height, and each was called lord.
units.literal: Moreover among the four hoary elders of South Mountain were Lord Yuan and Lord Xia Huang, who concealed their radiance; the age praised their loftiness, and all were styled lord.

units.zh: 然則公者仁德之正號，不必三事大夫也。
units.en: So "lord" is the proper honor for humane excellence, not reserved for ministers of the three bureaus.
units.literal: Thus "lord" is the correct title for humane virtue; one need not be a minister of the three departments.

units.zh: 昔東海於公僅有一節，猶或戒鄉人侈其門閭，矧乃鄭公之德，而無駟牡之路！
units.en: Even Yu Gong of Donghai, with a single good turn, told his neighbors to broaden his gate—how much more should we for Master Zheng's virtue, when his lane could not fit a team of four!
units.literal: Formerly Yu Gong of the Eastern Sea had only one good deed, yet he warned his fellow villagers to widen his gate; how much more Lord Zheng's virtue—and no road for a four-horse carriage!

units.zh: 靈帝末，黨禁解，大將軍何進聞而辟之。
units.en: Near the end of Lingdi's reign the ban ended; He Jin the general-in-chief heard of him and called him in.
units.literal: At the end of the Ling Emperor's reign the partisan prohibition was lifted; the general-in-chief He Jin heard of him and summoned him.

units.zh: 與吏部尚書江湛、太子左率袁淑善，淑薦之於始興王濬，濬深引納焉。
units.en: He was close to Minister of the Civil Service Jiang Zhan and the heir's left leader Yuan Shu; Shu recommended him to Prince Jun of Shixing, and Jun took him in warmly.
units.literal: He was on good terms with Minister of the Civil Service Jiang Zhan and Left Leader of the Heir's Household Yuan Shu; Shu recommended him to Prince Jun of Shixing, and Jun warmly received him.

units.zh: 樂藹字蔚遠，南陽淯陽人，晉尚書令廣之六世孫，世居江陵。
units.en: Yue Ai, styled Weiyuan, came from Yuyang in Nanyang, sixth from Jin's Director Guang; his line lived in Jiangling.
units.literal: Yue Ai, styled Weiyuan, was a native of Yuyang in Nanyang, sixth-generation descendant of Jin's Director of the Masters of Writing Guang, his family long in Jiangling.

units.zh: 數百年後，乃有王弼。
units.en: Several hundred years later came Wang Bi.
units.literal: Several hundred years later there was Wang Bi.

units.zh: 若謂易道盡於王弼，方須大論，意者無乃仁智殊見。
units.en: If one says the Way of the Changes is fully contained in Wang Bi, a great debate is needed; perhaps benevolence and wisdom simply see differently.
units.literal: If one says the Way of the Changes is exhausted in Wang Bi, then a great discussion is needed; perhaps benevolence and wisdom see differently.

units.zh: 晉太興四年，太常荀崧請置《周易》鄭玄注博士，行乎前代，于時政由王、庾，皆俊神清識，能言玄遠，捨輔嗣而用康成，豈其妄然。
units.en: In the fourth year of Taixing of Jin, Minister of Ceremonies Xun Song requested an Erudite for Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Book of Changes. This had been practiced in former generations; at that time government was in the hands of the Wang and Yu clans—all brilliant men of clear understanding, able to discourse on the abstruse. They set aside Wang Bi and used Zheng Xuan—how could this have been reckless?
units.literal: In the fourth year of Taixing of Jin, Minister of Ceremonies Xun Song requested establishment of an Erudite for Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Book of Changes. This was practiced in former generations; at that time government was in the hands of the Wang and Yu clans—all were brilliant spirits with clear understanding, able to speak of the abstruse and far-reaching. They set aside Fusi and used Kangcheng—how could this have been reckless?

units.zh: 時國學置鄭王《易》，杜服《春秋》，何氏《公羊》，麋氏《穀梁》，鄭玄《孝經》。
units.en: At that time the Imperial University taught Zheng and Wang commentaries on the Changes, Du and Fu on the Spring and Autumn, the He clan on the Gongyang, the Mi clan on the Guliang, and Zheng Xuan on the Classic of Filial Piety.
units.literal: At that time the Imperial University established Zheng and Wang commentaries on the Changes, Du and Fu on the Spring and Autumn, the He clan on the Gongyang, the Mi clan on the Guliang, and Zheng Xuan on the Classic of Filial Piety.

units.zh: 逮顏延之爲祭酒，黜鄭置王，意在貴玄，事成敗儒。
units.en: When Yan Yanzhi became Libationer, he dismissed Zheng and established Wang; the intent was to honor the abstruse school, and the result was a setback for Confucian learning.
units.literal: When Yan Yanzhi became Libationer, he dismissed Zheng and established Wang; the intent was to honor the abstruse, and the result was defeat for the Confucians.

units.zh: 王濟云弼所悟者多，何必能頓廢前儒。
units.en: Wang Ji said that Bi understood a great deal, but why must one suddenly abolish the earlier Confucians?
units.literal: Wang Ji said that what Bi understood was much, but why must one suddenly abolish the earlier Confucians?

units.zh: 太元立王肅易，當以在玄、弼之閒。
units.en: In the Taiyuan era Wang Su's Changes was established; it should be placed between Zheng Xuan and Wang Bi.
units.literal: In Taiyuan Wang Su's Changes was established; it should be placed between Xuan and Bi.

units.zh: 元嘉建學之始，玄、弼兩立。
units.en: When the school was established at the beginning of Yuanjia, Zheng Xuan and Wang Bi were both taught.
units.literal: At the beginning of establishing the school in Yuanjia, Xuan and Bi were both established.

units.zh: 且弼於注經中已舉《繫辭》，故不復別注。
units.en: Moreover, Wang Bi in his commentary on the classic already cited the Appended Phrases and therefore did not comment on them separately.
units.literal: Moreover, Bi in commenting on the classic already cited the Appended Phrases, and therefore did not comment on them separately.

units.zh: 今若專取弼《易》，則《繫》說無注。
units.en: If one now exclusively adopts Wang Bi's Changes, then the Appended Phrases will have no commentary.
units.literal: If one now exclusively takes Bi's Changes, then the Appended Phrases commentary has no annotation.

units.zh: 列傳第十六 謝瞻孔琳之
units.en: Biography 16: Xie Zhan and Kong Linzhi
units.literal: Biography 16: Xie Zhan, Kong Linzhi

units.zh: 謝瞻，字宣遠，一名簷，字通遠，陳郡陽夏人，衛將軍晦第三兄也。
units.en: Xie Zhan, whose courtesy name was Xuanyuan—he was also known as Yan, with the alternative courtesy name Tongyuan—came from Yangxia in Chen Commandery and was the third elder brother of Xie Hui, General of the Guard.
units.literal: Xie Zhan, courtesy name Xuanyuan, also called Yan with the alternative courtesy name Tongyuan, was a native of Yangxia in Chen Commandery and the third elder brother of General of the Guard Xie Hui.

units.zh: 年六歲，能屬文，為《紫石英贊》、《果然詩》，當時才士，莫不歎異。
units.en: At six he could already compose literary pieces, including "In Praise of Amethyst Quartz" and "The Guoran Poem," and every gifted writer of the time marveled at him.
units.literal: At the age of six he could compose literary works, writing "In Praise of Amethyst Quartz" and "The Guoran Poem"; the talented men of the day all sighed in wonder.

units.zh: 瞻善於文章，辭采之美，與族叔混、族弟靈運相抗。
units.en: Zhan was a gifted writer; the brilliance of his style rivaled that of his clansman Hun and his younger kinsman Lingyun.
units.literal: Zhan excelled at literary composition; the beauty of his diction matched that of his clansman Hun and his younger clansman Lingyun.

units.zh: 初為桓偉安西參軍，楚台秘書郎。
units.en: He began his career as a staff officer under Huan Wei in the Anxi command and later became Secretary Gentleman in the Chu court.
units.literal: He first served as staff officer to Huan Wei in the Anxi command, then as Secretary Gentleman in the Chu regime.

units.zh: 劉弟柳為吳郡，將姊俱行，瞻不能違，解職隨從，為柳建威長史。
units.en: When Lady Liu's brother Liu Liu was appointed governor of Wu and took their elder sister along, Zhan could not bring himself to stay behind; he resigned and went with them, serving Liu as chief clerk of the Jianwei command.
units.literal: When Lady Liu's younger brother Liu Liu became governor of Wu Commandery and took their elder sister with him, Zhan could not refuse and resigned his post to follow, serving Liu as Chief Clerk of the Jianwei command.

units.zh: 尋為高祖鎮軍、琅邪王大司馬參軍，轉主簿，安成相，中書侍郎，宋國中書、黃門侍郎，相國從事中郎。
units.en: He was soon appointed staff officer to Emperor Gaozu's Zhenjun Army and to the Prince of Langye as Grand Marshal, then served successively as chief clerk, administrator of Ancheng, gentleman of the palace secretariat, secretariat and yellow gate gentleman of the Song state, and attendant of the chancellor of state.
units.literal: Soon afterward he became a staff officer to the Zhenjun Army and to the Prince of Langye as Grand Marshal, then chief clerk, Administrator of Ancheng, Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat, Secretariat and Yellow Gate Gentleman of the Song state, and Attendant of the Chancellor of State.

units.zh: 高祖以瞻為吳興郡，又自陳請，乃為豫章太守。
units.en: Emperor Gaozu appointed Zhan to Wuxing Commandery, but Zhan petitioned again on his own behalf and was instead made administrator of Yuzhang.
units.literal: Emperor Gaozu appointed Zhan to Wuxing Commandery; he petitioned again on his own behalf and was then made Administrator of Yuzhang.

units.zh: 瞻幼孤，叔母劉撫養有恩紀，兄弟事之，同於至親。
units.en: Zhan was orphaned young; his aunt by marriage, the Liu lady, raised him with devoted care, and he and his brothers treated her exactly as they would their own parents.
units.literal: Zhan lost his father in childhood; his aunt by marriage, Lady Liu, raised him with devoted kindness, and he and his brothers served her as they would their closest kin.

units.zh: 時瞻在家，驚駭謂晦曰：「汝名位未多，而人歸趣乃爾。
units.en: Zhan was at home at the time. Alarmed, he said to Hui, "Your rank and title are still modest, yet people are flocking to you like this.
units.literal: Zhan was then at home and, startled and alarmed, said to Hui, "Your rank and title are not yet great, yet people flock to you like this.

units.zh: 吾家以素退為業，不願干預時事，交遊不過親朋，而汝遂勢傾朝野，此豈門戶之福邪？」
units.en: Our family has always made a virtue of modest retirement; we do not wish to meddle in public affairs, and our circle extends no farther than kin and friends—yet you have come to dominate court and countryside alike. Can this truly be a blessing for our house?"
units.literal: Our family has made plain withdrawal its calling; we do not wish to meddle in the affairs of the age, and our acquaintances extend no farther than kin and friends—yet you have come to sway court and countryside. Is this really a blessing for our house?"

units.zh: 乃籬隔門庭，曰：「吾不忍見此。」
units.en: He then put up a hedge to screen off the courtyard, saying, "I cannot bear to look upon this."
units.literal: He then fenced off the courtyard with a hedge, saying, "I cannot bear to see this."

units.zh: 及還彭城，言于高祖曰：「臣本素士，父、祖位不過二千石。
units.en: When he returned to Pengcheng he told Emperor Gaozu, "I was originally a man of no distinction; my father and grandfather never rose above the two-thousand-dan rank.
units.literal: When he returned to Pengcheng he spoke to Emperor Gaozu, saying, "Your servant was originally a plain scholar; my father and grandfather held posts no higher than the two-thousand-dan rank.

units.zh: 弟年始三十，志用凡近，榮冠台府，位任顯密，福過災生，其應無遠。
units.en: My brother has only just turned thirty; his talents and ambitions are unremarkable, yet his honors outshine the whole regime and his offices are weighty and exposed. When fortune runs too high, disaster follows—and that day cannot be far off.
units.literal: My brother has only just turned thirty; his aims and abilities are ordinary, yet his glory tops the regime and his office is conspicuous and weighty. When good fortune exceeds its measure, disaster is born—the consequence cannot be far off.

units.zh: 特乞降黜，以保衰門。」
units.en: I beg that he be demoted and removed from office, so that our declining house may be spared."
units.literal: I beg especially that he be demoted and removed from office, to preserve our declining house."

units.zh: 前後屢陳。
units.en: He made this plea again and again.
units.literal: He submitted such petitions repeatedly.

units.zh: 晦或以朝廷密事語瞻，瞻輒向親舊陳說，以為笑戲，以絕其言。
units.en: When Hui confided court secrets to him, Zhan would promptly repeat them to relatives and old friends as a joke, so as to put an end to such disclosures.
units.literal: Hui would sometimes tell Zhan confidential matters of the court; Zhan would at once repeat them to kin and old friends as a jest, to cut off such talk.

units.zh: 永初二年，在郡遇疾，不肯自治，幸於不永。
units.en: In the second year of Yongchu he fell ill while serving in his commandery; he refused medical care, hoping his life would not be prolonged.
units.literal: In the second year of Yongchu, while in his commandery he fell ill; he refused to treat himself, hoping his life would not be long.

units.zh: 晦聞疾奔往，瞻見之，曰：「汝為國大臣，又總戎重，萬里遠出，必生疑謗。」
units.en: When Hui heard of his illness he rushed to his side. Zhan saw him and said, "You are a chief minister of state and hold supreme military authority; to travel a thousand li on such an errand is bound to invite suspicion and slander."
units.literal: Hearing of the illness, Hui rushed to him; when Zhan saw him he said, "You are a great minister of state and also hold overall military authority; to travel a thousand li on such an errand is sure to breed suspicion and slander."

units.zh: 瞻疾篤還都，高祖以晦禁旅，不得出宿，使瞻居於晉南郡公主婿羊賁故第，在領軍府東門。
units.en: When Zhan's illness grew grave he returned to the capital. Because Hui commanded the palace guard and could not stay away overnight, Emperor Gaozu had Zhan lodged in the former residence of Yang Ben, son-in-law of the Jin Princess of Nan Commandery, east of the headquarters of the General of the Guards.
units.literal: When Zhan's illness grew grave he returned to the capital. Because Hui commanded the palace guard and could not lodge outside, Emperor Gaozu had Zhan stay in the former residence of Yang Ben, son-in-law of the Jin Princess of Nan Commandery, east of the General of the Guards headquarters.

units.zh: 瞻曰：「吾有先人弊廬，何為於此！」
units.en: Zhan said, "I have my forefathers' humble house—why should I stay here?"
units.literal: Zhan said, "I have my forefathers' humble dwelling—why should I be here!"

units.zh: 臨終，遣晦書曰：「吾得啟體幸全，歸骨山足，亦何所多恨。
units.en: On his deathbed he sent Hui a letter: "I have been fortunate to leave this world with my body whole and to return my bones to the hills—what more could I regret?
units.literal: On his deathbed he sent Hui a letter saying, "I have been fortunate to leave my body whole and to return my bones to the foot of the hills—what more is there to regret?

units.zh: 弟思自勉厲，為國為家。」
units.en: Brother, strive to discipline yourself—for the sake of the state and our house."
units.literal: Brother, strive to urge yourself on—for the state and for the family."

units.zh: 遂卒，時年三十五。
units.en: He died soon after, at the age of thirty-five.
units.literal: He then died, at the age of thirty-five.

units.zh: 乃與晦、曜、弘微等共遊戲，使瞻與靈運共車；
units.en: He then arranged outings with Hui, Yao, Hongwei, and the others and had Zhan share a carriage with Lingyun.
units.literal: He then joined Hui, Yao, Hongwei, and the others in shared outings and had Zhan ride in the same carriage as Lingyun.

units.zh: 靈運登車，便商較人物，瞻謂之曰：「秘書早亡，談者亦互有同異。」
units.en: The moment Lingyun got into the carriage he began ranking people's merits and faults. Zhan said to him, "The secretary gentleman died young, and even those who speak of him disagree among themselves."
units.literal: As soon as Lingyun boarded the carriage he began comparing people's merits; Zhan said to him, "The Secretary Gentleman died young, and those who discuss him also differ among themselves."

units.zh: 靈運默然，言論自此衰止。
units.en: Lingyun fell silent, and from that day his habit of judging others faded away.
units.literal: Lingyun fell silent, and from then on such talk dwindled and ceased.

units.zh: 弟晦時為宋台右衛，權遇已重，于彭城還都迎家，賓客輻輳，門巷填咽。
units.en: His younger brother Hui then held the post of Right Guard in the Song regime, and his influence was already formidable. When he returned from Pengcheng to the capital to bring the family home, guests thronged about him until the lanes before his gate were impassable.
units.literal: His younger brother Hui was then Right Guard of the Song regime; his power and favor were already great. Returning from Pengcheng to the capital to fetch the family, guests converged like wheel spokes and the lanes before his gate were choked.

units.zh: 弟㬭，字宣鏡，幼有殊行。
units.en: His younger brother Jiao, whose courtesy name was Xuanjing, showed exceptional conduct from childhood.
units.literal: His younger brother Jiao, courtesy name Xuanjing, showed extraordinary conduct from childhood.

units.zh: 晦遂建佐命之功，任寄隆重，瞻愈憂懼。
units.en: Hui went on to earn merit in establishing the new dynasty, and the trust placed in him grew ever heavier; Zhan's anxiety only deepened.
units.literal: Hui then achieved merit in aiding the founding mandate; his commission and trust grew weighty, and Zhan grew ever more anxious and afraid.

units.zh: 謂瞻曰：「非汝莫能。」
units.en: He said to Zhan, "No one but you can manage this."
units.literal: He said to Zhan, "No one but you can do it."

units.zh: 而趙亦有公孫龍為堅白同異之辯，劇子之言；
units.en: Zhao also had Gongsun Long, with his debates on "hard and white" and "sameness and difference," as well as the sayings of Master Ju;
units.literal: Zhao also had Gongsun Long, who debated 'hard and white' and 'sameness and difference,' and the words of Master Ju;

units.zh: 《宋書·止足傳》有羊欣、王微，咸其流亞。
units.en: The Song History "Biography of Knowing Sufficiency" has Yang Xin and Wang Wei—both of that stream.
units.literal: The Song History "Biography of Knowing Sufficiency" has Yang Xin and Wang Wei—both of that stream.

units.zh: 祖敞，晉度支尚書，父茂度，宋金紫光祿大夫。
units.en: His grandfather Chang had been Jin revenue superintendent; his father Maodu, a Song household minister with the purple-gold seal.
units.literal: His grandfather Chang was revenue superintendent of Jin; his father Maodu was household minister with the purple-gold seal under the Song.

units.zh: 宋國建，奉常鄭鮮之舉為博士，仍遷世子舍人。
units.en: After the Song state was founded, Zheng Xianzhi, Director of Ceremonies, recommended him as Erudite, and he was soon transferred to Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: When the State of Song was established, Director of Ceremonies Zheng Xianzhi recommended him as Erudite; he was then moved to Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 高祖受命，補太子舍人。
units.en: When the Founder took the throne, Yanzhi was appointed Attendant of the Crown Prince.
units.literal: When the Founder received the Mandate, he was appointed Attendant of the Crown Prince.
